title.zh: 卷一百三十八 列傳第二十五: 康里脫脫 燕鐵木兒 伯顏 馬札兒台 脫脫
title.en: Volume 138 Biographies 25: Kanglituotuo, El Temür, Bayan, Mazhaertai, Toqto'a
title.raw: 卷一百三十八 列傳第二十五: 康里脫脫 燕鐵木兒 伯顏 馬札兒台 脫脫 Volume 138 Biographies 25: Kanglituotuo, El Temür, Bayan, Mazhaertai, Toqto'a

sentences.zh: 康里脱脱

translations.literal: Kangli Tuotuo
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo of the Kangli

sentences.zh: 康里脫脫，父曰牙牙，由康國王封雲中王，阿沙不花之弟也。

translations.literal: Kangli Tuotuo—his father was called Yaya; from the kingship of Kang he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yunzhong; he was the younger brother of Asha Buhua.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo of the Kangli clan was the son of Yaya, who had been enfeoffed as Prince of Yunzhong after holding the kingship of Kang and was the younger brother of Asha Buhua.

sentences.zh: 脫脫姿貌魁梧，少時從其兄斡禿蠻獵於燕南，斡禿蠻使歸獻所獲，世祖見其骨氣沉雄，步履莊重，歎曰：「後日大用之才，已生於今。」

translations.literal: Tuotuo's bearing and appearance were imposing and tall. In his youth he followed his elder brother Otuman hunting south of Yan. Otuman had him return to present what they had taken. The Founding Emperor saw that his bone and spirit were deep and commanding and his gait solemn and measured, and sighed: "The talent for great employment in days to come has already been born in our time."
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo was tall and powerfully built. As a young man he accompanied his elder brother Otuman on hunts in the region south of Yan. Otuman sent him back to court with their quarry. Kublai, noting his forceful bearing and measured stride, exclaimed that a man fit for high office had already appeared in his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 即命入宿衛。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered him to enter the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately enrolled him in the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 成宗初，丞相伯顏在北鄙，脫脫奉詔以名鷹賜伯顏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chengzong's reign, the chief councillor Bayan was on the northern frontier; Tuotuo received an edict to present a famous hawk to Bayan as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Chengzong, Chief Councillor Bayan was stationed on the northern frontier, and Tuotuo was ordered to present him with a prized hawk.

sentences.zh: 伯顏見之，驚問曰：「汝為何人子？」

translations.literal: When Bayan saw him, he asked in surprise: "Whose son are you?"
translations.idiomatic: Bayan was startled when he saw him and asked, "Whose son are you?"

sentences.zh: 脫脫以實對，伯顏語之曰：「吾老矣，他日可大用者，未見汝比。」

translations.literal: Tuotuo answered truthfully. Bayan said to him: "I am old; among those who may be greatly employed hereafter, I have not seen your equal."
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo told him the truth. Bayan said, "I am growing old, and I have not met anyone your equal among those who may yet rise to great office."

sentences.zh: 大德三年，武宗以皇子撫軍北鄙，脫脫從行。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade, Wuzong as imperial prince pacified the army on the northern frontier, and Tuotuo accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1299, when Prince Wuzong took command on the northern frontier, Tuotuo went with him.

sentences.zh: 五年，叛王海都犯邊，脫脫從武宗討之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the rebel prince Haidu invaded the border; Tuotuo followed Wuzong to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1301, when the rebel prince Haidu raided the frontier, Tuotuo joined Wuzong's campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 師次杭海，進擊海都，大破其衆，脫脫手斮一士之首，連背胛以獻，武宗壯之。

translations.literal: The army halted at Hanghai and advanced to attack Haidu, routing his forces. Tuotuo with his own hand cut off a soldier's head, together with the shoulder blade attached, and presented it; Wuzong admired this.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped at Hanghai and advanced on Haidu, inflicting a crushing defeat. Tuotuo personally severed an enemy soldier's head, shoulder blade still attached, and presented it as a trophy. Wuzong was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 兵之始交也，武宗銳欲出戰，脫脫執轡力諫，武宗怒，揮鞭抶其手，不退，乃止。

translations.literal: When the armies first engaged, Wuzong was eager to go out and fight. Tuotuo seized the reins and strongly remonstrated. Wuzong was angry and lashed his hand with a whip, but Tuotuo did not withdraw, and Wuzong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the first clash, Wuzong was eager to join the fighting himself. Tuotuo seized the reins and pleaded with him not to. Enraged, Wuzong struck his hand with a whip, but Tuotuo would not yield, and the prince finally desisted.

sentences.zh: 已而武宗與大將朶兒荅哈語及之，朶兒荅哈曰：「太子在軍中，如身有首，如衣有領，脫有不虞，衆安所附？

translations.literal: Afterward Wuzong spoke of this with the great general Doreqa. Doreqa said: "When the heir apparent is in the army, it is like a body having a head or a garment having a collar. If something untoward should occur, to whom would the multitude attach itself?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wuzong mentioned the incident to the general Doreqa, Doreqa said, "The heir apparent in the field is like a body without which the head cannot stand, or a robe without a collar. If anything should befall him, whom would the troops follow?

sentences.zh: 脫脫之諫可謂忠矣。」

translations.literal: Tuotuo's remonstrance may be called loyal."
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo's counsel was nothing if not loyal."

sentences.zh: 武宗深然之。

translations.literal: Wuzong deeply agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 成宗大漸，丞相哈剌哈孫荅剌罕稱疾卧直廬中。

translations.literal: When Chengzong was gravely ill, Chief Councillor Qalaqush Darqan feigned illness and lay in the duty chamber.
translations.idiomatic: As Chengzong lay dying, Chief Councillor Qalaqush Darqan claimed illness and remained in the palace duty quarters.

sentences.zh: 脫脫適以使事至京師，即俾馳告武宗以國恤，語在阿沙不花傳。

translations.literal: Tuotuo happened to be in the capital on a mission and was immediately sent post-haste to inform Wuzong of the national bereavement; the account is in the biography of Asha Buhua.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo happened to be in the capital on official business and was immediately dispatched to inform Wuzong of the emperor's death; the fuller account appears in the biography of Asha Buhua.

sentences.zh: 時仁宗奉興聖太后至自懷孟，既定內難，而太后以兩太子星命付陰陽家推筭，問所宜立者，曰：「重光大荒落有災，旃蒙作噩長久。」

translations.literal: At that time Renzong had escorted Empress Dowager Xingsheng from Huaimei. After the internal strife was settled, the empress dowager entrusted the two princes' natal stars to yin-yang masters for calculation and asked which ought to be enthroned. They said: "Chongguang, Dahuangluo—there will be disaster; Zhanmeng, Zuoe—long endurance."
translations.idiomatic: Renzong had meanwhile brought Empress Dowager Xingsheng from Huaimei. Once the internal crisis was settled, the empress dowager had astrologers calculate the fates of the two princes and asked which should succeed. They replied that Wuzong's cyclical year sign foretold calamity, while Renzong's sign promised longevity.

sentences.zh: 重光為武宗年幹，旃蒙為仁宗年幹。

translations.literal: Chongguang was Wuzong's year stem; Zhanmeng was Renzong's year stem.
translations.idiomatic: Chongguang was the cyclical designation for Wuzong's birth year, and Zhanmeng for Renzong's.

sentences.zh: 於是太后頗惑其言，遣近臣朶耳諭旨武宗曰：「汝兄弟二人皆我所出，豈有親疏？

translations.literal: Thereupon the empress dowager was quite swayed by their words and sent a close attendant, Duo'er, to convey her intent to Wuzong, saying: "You two brothers were both born of me—how could there be closeness or distance?
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was much swayed and sent a close attendant named Duo'er to tell Wuzong, "Both of you are my sons—how could I favor one over the other?

sentences.zh: 陰陽家所言運祚修短，不容不思。」

translations.literal: What the yin-yang masters say about the length of fortune and fate cannot but be pondered."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the astrologers' words about the length of each reign cannot be ignored."

sentences.zh: 武宗聞之，默然，進脫脫而言曰：「我捍禦邊陲，勤勞十年，又次序居長，神器所歸， 灼然何疑。

translations.literal: When Wuzong heard this, he was silent, then summoned Tuotuo and said: "I have defended the frontier for ten years of toil, and moreover by order of succession I am the elder. To whom the regalia belongs is clear—what doubt is there?
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong listened in silence, then called Tuotuo and said, "I have spent ten years defending the frontier. I am the elder brother. The throne is plainly mine—what doubt can there be?

sentences.zh: 今太后以星命休咎為言，天道茫昧，誰能豫知？

translations.literal: Now the empress dowager speaks in terms of the stars' fortune and misfortune. The way of Heaven is obscure—who can foreknow?
translations.idiomatic: Now the empress dowager invokes the stars' verdict. Heaven's will is obscure—who can foresee it?

sentences.zh: 設使我即位之後，所設施者上合天心，下副民望，則雖一日之短，亦足垂名萬年，何可以陰陽之言而乖祖宗之託哉！

translations.literal: Suppose that after I take the throne, what I enact accords with Heaven's mind above and fulfills the people's hopes below—then even a reign of one day's brevity would suffice to leave a name for ten thousand years. How can one, on account of yin-yang talk, go against the entrustment of the ancestors!
translations.idiomatic: If, once I reign, my policies win Heaven's favor and the people's trust, then even a brief reign would secure my name for ages. How can I betray our ancestors' trust because of astrologers' words!

sentences.zh: 此蓋近日任事之臣，擅權專殺，恐我他日或治其罪，故為是奸謀動搖大本耳。

translations.literal: This is surely because recent ministers in office monopolize power and kill at will, fearing that I may one day punish their crimes, and therefore contrive this treacherous plot to shake the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: This is surely the work of ministers who have seized power and fear I will punish them once I reign—they have devised this plot to undermine the succession.

sentences.zh: 脫脫，汝為我往察事機，疾歸報我。」

translations.literal: Tuotuo, you go for me to investigate how matters stand and return quickly to report."
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo, go to the capital, learn how things stand, and return to me at once."

sentences.zh: 脫脫承命即行。

translations.literal: Tuotuo received the command and set out at once.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo obeyed and departed immediately.

sentences.zh: 武宗親率大軍由西道進，按灰由中道，床兀兒由東道，各以勁卒一萬從。

translations.literal: Wuzong personally led a great army advancing by the western route; Anqa by the central route; and Chen'er by the eastern route, each with ten thousand crack troops following.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong himself led the main force along the western route, with Anqa on the center and Chen'er on the east, each commanding ten thousand elite troops.

sentences.zh: 脫脫馳至大都，入見太后，道武宗所授旨以聞。

translations.literal: Tuotuo galloped to Dadu, entered to see the empress dowager, and reported the charge Wuzong had entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo rode post-haste to Dadu, audience with the empress dowager, and delivered Wuzong's message.

sentences.zh: 太后愕然曰：「修短之說雖出術家，為太子周思遠慮乃出我深愛。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said in astonishment: "Though the talk of long and short life comes from the masters of arts, to think far ahead for the heir apparent's sake proceeds from my deep love.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was startled and said, "The astrologers spoke of longevity, but my only aim was to think ahead for the heir apparent's sake, out of deep affection.

sentences.zh: 貪憝已除，宗王大臣議已定，太子不速來何為？」

translations.literal: The greedy and violent have already been removed; the imperial princes and great ministers have settled their deliberations. Why does the heir apparent not come quickly?"
translations.idiomatic: The plotters have been removed and the princes and ministers have already decided. Why does the heir apparent not hurry here?"

sentences.zh: 時諸王禿列等侍，咸曰：「臣下翊戴嗣君，無二心者。」

translations.literal: At that time the princes Tule and others were in attendance, and all said: "We subjects support and uphold the succeeding ruler—there is no second heart."
translations.idiomatic: The princes Tule and others who were present all declared, "We serve the successor with undivided loyalty."

sentences.zh: 既而太后、仁宗屏左右，留脫脫與語曰：「太子天性孝友，中外屬望。

translations.literal: Then the empress dowager and Renzong dismissed those on either side and kept Tuotuo to speak with him, saying: "The heir apparent is by nature filial and friendly; within and without, all look to him.
translations.idiomatic: Then the empress dowager and Renzong dismissed their attendants and spoke privately with Tuotuo. "The heir apparent is by nature dutiful and affectionate," they said. "Everyone looks to him.

sentences.zh: 今聞汝所致言，殆有讒間。

translations.literal: Now hearing what you have reported, there is probably slander creating estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: From what you report, it seems someone has been sowing discord between the brothers.

sentences.zh: 汝歸速為我彌縫闕失，使我骨肉無間，相見怡愉，則汝功為不細矣。」

translations.literal: When you return, quickly mend our faults for us, so that our flesh and bone have no rift and meet in ease and joy—then your merit will be no small thing."
translations.idiomatic: Return quickly and repair this breach, so that the brothers meet in harmony. Your service will not be forgotten."

sentences.zh: 脫脫頓首謝曰：「太母、太弟不煩過慮，臣侍藩邸歷年，頗見信任，今歸當即推誠竭忠以開釋太子。

translations.literal: Tuotuo bowed his head and thanked them, saying: "Grand Empress and Grand Younger Brother, do not trouble yourselves with excessive worry. I have served the princely establishment for years and have seen considerable trust. Now on my return I shall at once employ sincerity and exhaust loyalty to clear away the heir apparent's doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo kowtowed and said, "Grand Empress, Grand Younger Brother—please do not worry unduly. I have served the heir apparent for years and enjoy his trust. I shall return and speak to him frankly to dispel his suspicions.

sentences.zh: 後日三宮共處，靡有嫌隙，斯為脫脫所報效矣。」

translations.literal: Hereafter, when the three palaces dwell together without the least suspicion, that will be Tuotuo's repayment of service."
translations.idiomatic: If the three courts can live together without rancor, that will be my reward enough."

sentences.zh: 先是，太后以武宗遲迴不至，已遣阿沙不花往道諸王群臣推戴之意。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Wuzong delayed and did not arrive, the empress dowager had already sent Asha Buhua to convey to the princes and ministers the intent to support and enthrone him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Wuzong had been slow to come, the empress dowager had sent Asha Buhua to inform the princes and ministers of their resolve to enthrone him.

sentences.zh: 及是脫脫繼往，行至旺古察，武宗在馬轎中望見其來，趣使疾馳，與之共載。

translations.literal: At this time Tuotuo followed after. When he reached Wanggucha, Wuzong, in his horse litter, saw him coming from afar and urged him to gallop swiftly; they rode together in the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo followed. At Wanggucha, Wuzong, riding in his litter, saw him approach and ordered him to hurry; they rode together in the same carriage.

sentences.zh: 脫脫具致太后、仁宗之語，武宗乃大感悟，釋然無疑。

translations.literal: Tuotuo fully conveyed the words of the empress dowager and Renzong. Wuzong then greatly came to understanding, and his doubts were entirely released.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo repeated everything the empress dowager and Renzong had said. Wuzong was deeply moved and laid his doubts to rest.

sentences.zh: 遂遣阿沙不花還報。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent Asha Buhua back with a report.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Asha Buhua back with his reply.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即日命駕奉迎于上都。

translations.literal: Renzong that same day ordered his carriage to go welcome him at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Renzong set out to welcome him at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 武宗正位宸極，尊太后為皇太后，立仁宗為皇太子，三宮協和，脫脫兄弟之力為多。

translations.literal: Wuzong took the correct position upon the imperial throne, honored the empress dowager as empress dowager, and established Renzong as heir apparent. The three palaces were in harmony—much of this was due to the efforts of Tuotuo and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong ascended the throne, honored the empress dowager, and named Renzong heir apparent. Harmony among the three courts owed much to Tuotuo and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 脫脫之至京師也，武宗嘗命其同知樞密院，比還，問曾視事否，脫脫對曰：「今正殿未御，宗親未見，為扈從之臣攙取名位，誠恐有累聖德，是以未敢祗事。」

translations.literal: When Tuotuo had come to the capital, Wuzong had once ordered him to serve as associate administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs. When he returned, Wuzong asked whether he had taken up his duties. Tuotuo replied: "Now the main hall has not yet been occupied, and the imperial kin have not yet been received. For a attendant minister to seize a title and post—I truly fear it would burden the sage virtue; therefore I did not dare to accept the office."
translations.idiomatic: While Tuotuo was in the capital, Wuzong had appointed him associate administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs. On his return, Wuzong asked whether he had assumed the post. Tuotuo replied, "The throne has not yet been formally taken and the imperial clan has not been received. For a companion to seize an office now would tarnish Your Majesty's virtue, so I dared not accept it."

sentences.zh: 武宗嘉歎久之。

translations.literal: Wuzong praised and sighed over this for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 知樞密院只兒哈忽在潛邸時嘗有不遜語，將置于法，脫脫諫曰：「陛下新正位，大信未立而輒行誅戮，知者以為彼自有罪，不知者以為報仇，恐人人自危。

translations.literal: The administrator of military affairs Jirhahu, while Wuzong was still heir apparent, had once spoken disrespectfully and was about to be punished by law. Tuotuo remonstrated: "Your Majesty has newly taken the throne; great trust is not yet established, and to execute punishment at once—those who know will think he had his own guilt, but those who do not will think it revenge. I fear everyone will feel endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Jirhahu, administrator of military affairs, had once spoken disrespectfully to Wuzong when he was still heir apparent and was to be punished. Tuotuo urged, "Your Majesty has just ascended the throne. If you execute him before trust is established, the informed will see justice, but others will see revenge—and everyone will live in fear.

sentences.zh: 況只兒哈忽習於先朝典故，今固不可少也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Jirhahu is versed in the precedents of the former court—he truly cannot be dispensed with now."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Jirhahu knows the precedents of the previous reign and is indispensable."

sentences.zh: 乃宥之。

translations.literal: He was thereupon pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong spared him.

sentences.zh: 繼海都而王者曰察八兒，素服武宗威名，至是率諸王內附，詔特設宴於大庭。

translations.literal: Chapar, who succeeded Haidu as king, had always submitted to Wuzong's martial renown; at this time he led the princes in submitting to the interior, and an edict specially ordered a banquet in the great court.
translations.idiomatic: Chapar, who had succeeded Haidu, had long respected Wuzong's military reputation. He now led the princes in submission, and the court ordered a grand banquet in their honor.

sentences.zh: 故事，凡大宴，必命近臣敷宣王度，以為告戒。

translations.literal: By precedent, at every great banquet the emperor must order a close minister to expound and proclaim the kingly norms as admonition and warning.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, at every great banquet a close minister was charged to expound the principles of kingship as a moral lesson.

sentences.zh: 脫脫薦只兒哈忽，令具其言以進，果稱旨。

translations.literal: Tuotuo recommended Jirhahu and had him prepare his words to present; they indeed accorded with the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo recommended Jirhahu and had him draft the address, which pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 武宗歎曰：「博爾忽、博爾朮前朝人傑，脫脫今世人傑也。」

translations.literal: Wuzong sighed and said: "Boroqul and Boro'e were eminent men of the former court; Tuotuo is an eminent man of the present age."
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong exclaimed, "Boroqul and Boro'e were the great men of the founding generation; Tuotuo is the great man of our age."

sentences.zh: 即以所進之言授脫脫。

translations.literal: He thereupon entrusted to Tuotuo the words that had been presented.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Tuotuo deliver the address himself.

sentences.zh: 及諸王大臣被宴服就列，脫脫即席陳西北諸藩始終離合之由、去逆效順之義，辭旨明暢，聽者傾服。

translations.literal: When the princes and great ministers, in banquet dress, took their places, Tuotuo from his seat set forth the reasons for the northwestern fiefs' successive union and separation from beginning to end, and the meaning of abandoning rebellion and submitting in loyalty. His language was clear and fluent, and the listeners were won over.
translations.idiomatic: When the princes and ministers took their places in banquet dress, Tuotuo rose and explained why the northwestern princes had wavered and why they should now submit. His speech was lucid and compelling, and all were persuaded.

sentences.zh: 自同知樞密院事進中書平章政事，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: From associate administrator of military affairs he was advanced to Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted from associate administrator of military affairs to Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 遷江南行臺御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋召拜錄軍國重事、中書左丞相。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Recorder of Weighty Affairs of Army and State and Left Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and appointed Recorder of Weighty Affairs of Army and State and Left Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 脫脫知無不言，言無不行，中外翕然稱為賢相。

translations.literal: Tuotuo knew nothing he did not speak of, and nothing he spoke of failed to be carried out; within and without, all harmoniously called him a worthy chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo spoke his mind on every matter and saw his counsel carried out. Court and country alike hailed him as a worthy chief minister.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，尚書省立，遷右丞相。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhida, when the Ministry of State Affairs was established, he was transferred to Right Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1310, when the Ministry of State Affairs was established, he was made Right Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 三寶奴等勸武宗立皇子為皇太子。

translations.literal: Sanbaonu and others urged Wuzong to establish his son as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Sanbaonu and others urged Wuzong to name his own son heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 脫脫方獵于柳林，遣使亟召之還。

translations.literal: Tuotuo was then hunting at Liulin; they sent messengers urgently to summon him back.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo was hunting at Liulin when messengers were sent to summon him back in haste.

sentences.zh: 三寶奴曰：「建儲議急，故相召耳。」

translations.literal: Sanbaonu said: "The deliberation on establishing the heir is urgent; therefore you were summoned."
translations.idiomatic: Sanbaonu said, "The question of the succession is urgent—that is why you were called."

sentences.zh: 脫脫驚曰：「何謂也？」

translations.literal: Tuotuo said in alarm: "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo was alarmed and asked, "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「皇子寖長，聖體近日倦勤，儲副所宜早定。」

translations.literal: He said: "The imperial son is gradually growing up; the sage person lately wearies of diligence. The heir designate ought to be settled early."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The prince is growing up, and His Majesty has lately wearied of affairs. The succession should be settled soon."

sentences.zh: 脫脫曰：「國家大計不可不慎。

translations.literal: Tuotuo said: "The great plan of the state cannot but be treated with caution.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo said, "The succession is a matter of the highest importance and must not be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 曩者太弟躬定大事，功在宗社，位居東宮，已有定命，自是兄弟叔姪世世相承，孰敢紊其序者！

translations.literal: Formerly the younger imperial brother personally settled the great affair; his merit was upon the altars of soil and grain; he occupies the Eastern Palace, and there is already a settled mandate. From this time forward brothers, uncles, and nephews succeed one another generation after generation—who would dare disorder this sequence!
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother settled the succession himself; his service to the dynasty earned him the Eastern Palace, and the order of succession is already fixed. Brothers and nephews are to succeed one another in turn—who would dare disturb that order!

sentences.zh: 我輩臣子，於國憲章縱不能有所匡贊，何可隳其成。」

translations.literal: We subjects, even if we cannot in the state's statutes and regulations offer some correction and support, how can we destroy what has been accomplished?"
translations.idiomatic: We ministers may be unable to improve the constitutional order, but we must not undo what has already been settled."

sentences.zh: 三寶奴曰：「今日兄已授弟，後日叔當授姪，能保之乎？」

translations.literal: Sanbaonu said: "Today the elder has given to the younger; tomorrow the uncle ought to give to the nephew—can that be guaranteed?"
translations.idiomatic: Sanbaonu said, "Today the elder brother yields to the younger; tomorrow the uncle must yield to the nephew—can you guarantee that?"

sentences.zh: 脫脫曰：「在我不可渝，彼失其信，天實鑒之。」

translations.literal: Tuotuo said: "On our side it cannot be altered; if the other side breaks faith, Heaven truly observes it."
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo replied, "Our side must not break faith. If others break theirs, Heaven will judge them."

sentences.zh: 三寶奴雖不以為然，而莫能奪其議也。

translations.literal: Although Sanbaonu did not consider this correct, he could not overturn Tuotuo's argument.
translations.idiomatic: Sanbaonu was unconvinced but could not prevail against him.

sentences.zh: 是時，尚書省賜予無節，遷敘無法，財用日耗，名爵日濫。

translations.literal: At this time the Ministry of State Affairs gave rewards without measure, promotions and demotions without method, expenditures daily depleted, and titles daily abused.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Ministry of State Affairs lavished rewards without restraint, promoted officials without rule, drained the treasury daily, and debased ranks without end.

sentences.zh: 脫脫進言曰：「爵賞者，帝王所以用人也。

translations.literal: Tuotuo advanced a memorial saying: "Titles and rewards are what emperors and kings use to employ men.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo submitted a memorial: "Titles and rewards are how emperors recruit and retain talent.

sentences.zh: 今爵及比德，賞及罔功，緩急之際何所賴乎！

translations.literal: Now titles reach those comparable in virtue, and rewards reach those without merit—in an hour of urgency, upon what can one rely!
translations.idiomatic: Now ranks go to the undeserving and rewards to the unmeritorious—when crisis comes, what will remain to offer?

sentences.zh: 中書所掌，錢糧、工役、選法、刑獄十有二事。

translations.literal: What the Secretariat administers comprises twelve matters: funds and grain, labor service, selection law, and penal prisons.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat oversees twelve domains: revenue, labor, appointments, and justice among them.

sentences.zh: 若從臣言，恪遵舊制，則臣願與諸賢黽勉從事。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty follows my words and scrupulously observes the old regulations, then I wish to exert myself diligently together with all the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will follow my counsel and restore the old regulations, I shall work diligently with my colleagues.

sentences.zh: 不然，用臣何補！」

translations.literal: Otherwise, of what use is employing me!"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, I am of no use to Your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 遂有詔俾濫受宣敕者赴所屬繳納。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered those who had improperly received patent letters of appointment to go to their respective offices and surrender them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed requiring all who had improperly received appointments to return them to the proper offices.

sentences.zh: 僥倖之路既塞，奔競之風頓衰。

translations.literal: Once the path of undeserved fortune was blocked, the wind of scrambling competition abruptly declined.
translations.idiomatic: With the path to easy advancement closed, the scramble for office sharply abated.

sentences.zh: 中臺有贓罰鈔五百萬緡，脫脫請出以賑孤寡老疾諸窮而無告者。

translations.literal: The Central Censorate had five million strings in confiscated and penal paper money; Tuotuo requested that it be disbursed to relieve the orphaned, widowed, aged, and ill, and all the destitute without anyone to appeal for them.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Censorate held five million strings in fines and confiscations. Tuotuo asked that it be distributed to orphans, widows, the aged, the sick, and others with no one to plead for them.

sentences.zh: 宗王南忽里部人告其主為不軌，脫脫辯其誣，抵告者罪。

translations.literal: A man of Prince Nanhuli's tribe reported his lord for misconduct; Tuotuo argued that it was false accusation and punished the accuser.
translations.idiomatic: A tribesman of Prince Nanhuli accused his lord of treason. Tuotuo proved the charge false and punished the accuser.

sentences.zh: 宗王牙忽禿徵其舊民於齊王八不沙部中，鄰境諸王欲奉齊王攻牙忽禿，齊王懼奔牙忽禿以避之，遂告齊王反。

translations.literal: Prince Yahutu summoned his former subjects from among the people of Prince Babusha of Qi. The neighboring princes wished to support the Prince of Qi to attack Yahutu. The Prince of Qi, in fear, fled to Yahutu to avoid this, and then reported that the Prince of Qi had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yahutu tried to reclaim subjects from Prince Babusha of Qi's domain. Neighboring princes proposed to support the Prince of Qi against Yahutu. The Prince of Qi, fearing attack, fled to Yahutu for protection, whereupon his enemies accused him of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 脫脫簿問得實，乃釋齊王而徙諸王于嶺南。

translations.literal: Tuotuo examined the registers and questioned witnesses until the facts were clear; he then released the Prince of Qi and transferred the other princes to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo investigated and found the truth, released the Prince of Qi, and banished the accusers to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 邊將脫火赤請以新軍萬人益宗王丑漢，廷議俾脫脫往給其資裝。

translations.literal: The frontier general Toqochi requested ten thousand men of the new army to reinforce Prince Chuhan. The court deliberated and ordered Tuotuo to go supply his funds and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier general Toqochi asked for ten thousand new troops to reinforce Prince Chuhan. The court decided to send Tuotuo to furnish supplies.

sentences.zh: 脫脫謂時方寧謐，不宜挑變生事，辭不行。

translations.literal: Tuotuo said that the time was now tranquil and one ought not provoke change and create trouble; he declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo argued that the realm was at peace and such a move might provoke trouble, and declined to go.

sentences.zh: 遂遣丞相禿忽魯等二人往給之， 幾以激變。

translations.literal: They then sent Chief Councillor Tughluq and two others to supply him—nearly provoking an uprising.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Tughluq and two others were sent instead—and nearly sparked a revolt.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，復為中書左丞相。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, he was again made Left Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1311 he was again appointed Left Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，眷待彌篤，欲使均逸于外，二月，拜江浙行省左丞相。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, his favor and treatment grew ever deeper. Wishing to let him enjoy ease abroad, in the second month he was appointed Left Grand Councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong succeeded, his favor for Tuotuo deepened. Wishing to give him a rest from court, in the second month he was appointed Left Grand Councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 下車，進父老問民利病，咸謂杭城故有便河通于江滸，堙廢已久，若疏鑿以通舟楫，物價必平。

translations.literal: Upon taking office, he advanced to the elders and asked about what benefited or harmed the people. All said that Hangzhou City formerly had a convenience canal communicating with the river's edge, long silted up and abandoned; if it were dredged and opened for boats, prices would surely be stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he consulted the local elders about the people's welfare. They all said that Hangzhou once had a canal to the river that had long been silted up; if dredged for shipping, prices would stabilize.

sentences.zh: 僚佐或難之，脫脫曰：「吾陛辭之日，密旨許以便宜行事。

translations.literal: Some subordinates objected. Tuotuo said: "On the day I took leave at court, a secret edict permitted me to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Some subordinates objected, but Tuotuo said, "When I took leave of the emperor, I received a secret authorization to act at my discretion.

sentences.zh: 民以為便，行之可也。」

translations.literal: The people regard it as convenient—it may be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: The people will benefit—let it be done."

sentences.zh: 俄有旨禁勿興土功，脫脫曰：「敬天莫先勤民，民蒙其利則災沴自弭，土功何尤。」

translations.literal: Soon there came an edict forbidding the undertaking of earthworks. Tuotuo said: "In honoring Heaven, nothing comes before working diligently for the people. If the people receive its benefit, calamities and pestilence will themselves be quelled—what fault is there in earthworks?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict forbade public works. Tuotuo replied, "The best way to honor Heaven is to serve the people. If they benefit, disasters will subside of themselves—what fault is there in this work?"

sentences.zh: 不一月而成。

translations.literal: In less than a month it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month it was finished.

sentences.zh: 是時，鐵木迭兒為丞相，欲固位取寵，乃議立仁宗子英宗為皇太子，而明宗以武宗子封周王，出鎮于雲南。

translations.literal: At this time Temuder was chief councillor; wishing to secure his position and win favor, he deliberated on establishing Renzong's son, Emperor Yingzong, as heir apparent, while Mingzong, as Wuzong's son, was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhou and sent out to garrison Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Temuder was then chief councillor and, seeking to secure his power, proposed making Renzong's son the future Yingzong heir apparent while enfeoffing Wuzong's son Mingzong as Prince of Zhou and posting him to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 又譖脫脫為武宗舊臣。

translations.literal: He also slandered Tuotuo as an old minister of Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: He also denounced Tuotuo as a partisan of Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 詔逮至京師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him arrested and brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him to the capital under arrest.

sentences.zh: 居數日，床兀兒、失列門傳兩宮旨諭脫脫曰：「初疑汝親於所事，故召汝。

translations.literal: After several days' residence, Chen'er and Shilie'men conveyed the intent of the two palaces to Tuotuo, saying: "At first we suspected you were close to those you served; therefore we summoned you.
translations.idiomatic: After several days, Chen'er and Shilie'men conveyed messages from the two palaces: "We first suspected you of loyalty to your former master, and therefore summoned you.

sentences.zh: 今察汝無他，其復還鎮。」

translations.literal: Now observing that you have no other intent, return again to your post."
translations.idiomatic: We now see you are blameless. Return to your post."

sentences.zh: 脫脫入謝太后曰：「臣雖被先帝知遇，而受太后及今上恩不為不深，豈敢昧所自乎。」

translations.literal: Tuotuo entered to thank the empress dowager, saying: "Although I was favored by the late emperor, the grace I have received from Your Majesty the Empress Dowager and the present sovereign is not shallow—how would I dare be ungrateful for my origins?"
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo went in to thank the empress dowager and said, "Though the late emperor favored me, the grace I owe Your Majesty and the present sovereign is no less deep. How could I forget where my loyalty lies?"

sentences.zh: 還江浙。

translations.literal: He returned to Jiang-Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Jiang-Zhe.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷江西行省左丞相。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Left Grand Councillor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Left Grand Councillor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 英宗嗣位，召拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Yingzong succeeded to the throne, Tuotuo was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong succeeded, Tuotuo was recalled and appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時帖赤先為大夫，陰忌之，奏改江南行臺御史大夫。

translations.literal: At that time Tiechi had previously been censor-in-chief and secretly envied him; he memorialized to change Tuotuo's post to Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Tiechi, who had previously served as censor-in-chief, secretly resented him and had him transferred to the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 復嗾言者劾其擅離職守，將徙之雲南，會帖赤伏誅，乃解。

translations.literal: He again incited memorialists to impeach Tuotuo for leaving his post without authorization and was about to transfer him to Yunnan; when Tiechi was executed, the matter was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: He then instigated accusers to charge Tuotuo with abandoning his post without leave and was about to banish him to Yunnan, but when Tiechi was executed the affair was dropped.

sentences.zh: 家居不出者五年。

translations.literal: He remained at home and did not go out for five years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement at home for five years.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年薨，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding he died; he was fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1327, at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 至正初，贈推誠全德守義佐運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封和寧王，諡忠獻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhizheng he was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Sincerely Upholds Complete Virtue, Guards Righteousness, and Assists the Dynasty; Grand Preceptor; Commissioner with Credentials Equal to the Three Dukes; and Upper Pillar of State; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Hening; posthumous name Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhizheng era he was posthumously honored as a founding minister, Grand Preceptor, Commissioner with Credentials Equal to the Three Dukes, and Upper Pillar of State, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Hening with the posthumous name Loyal and Dedicated.

sentences.zh: 脫脫嘗即宣德別墅延師以訓子，鄉人化之，皆向學。

translations.literal: Tuotuo once at his Xuande villa invited teachers to instruct his sons; the villagers were transformed by this and all turned toward learning.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo once invited teachers to his Xuande villa to educate his sons, and the example transformed the neighborhood so that all turned to study.

sentences.zh: 朝廷賜其精舍額曰景賢書院，為設學官。

translations.literal: The court granted his refined abode the plaque Jingxian Academy and established school officials for it.
translations.idiomatic: The court named his estate the Jingxian Academy and appointed official instructors.

sentences.zh: 其沒也，即其中祠焉。

translations.literal: When he died, a shrine was established within it for him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death a shrine was erected there in his honor.

sentences.zh: 子九人，其最顯者二人：曰鐵木兒塔識，曰達識帖睦邇，各有傳。

translations.literal: He had nine sons; the two most illustrious were called Temurtash and Dash Temur, each with his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons; the two most prominent were Temurtash and Dash Temur, each of whom has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 燕鐵木兒

translations.literal: El Temür
translations.idiomatic: El Temür

sentences.zh: 泰定帝崩于上都，丞相倒剌沙專政，宗室諸王脫脫、王禪附之，利於立幼。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiding died at Shangdu. Chief Councillor Toghto'a monopolized government. The imperial princes Tuotuo and Wangchan attached themselves to him, favoring the enthronement of a young ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiding died at Shangdu, Chief Councillor Toghto'a seized power. The princes Tuotuo and Wangchan supported him, preferring to enthrone a child emperor.

sentences.zh: 燕鐵木兒時緫環衛事，留大都，自以身受武宗寵拔之恩，其子宜纂大位，而一居朔漠，一處南陲，實天之所置，將以啟之。

translations.literal: El Temür then oversaw the palace guard duties and remained in Dadu. He considered that he himself had received Wuzong's favor and advancement, and that Wuzong's son ought to succeed to the great throne; yet one dwelt in the northern desert and one on the southern frontier—this was truly Heaven's placement, about to be opened by it.
translations.idiomatic: El Temür, who commanded the palace guard and remained in Dadu, believed that Wuzong's son was the rightful heir, having himself been raised by Wuzong's favor. With one prince in the north and one in the south, he saw Heaven's hand preparing the succession.

sentences.zh: 由是與公主察吉兒、族黨阿剌帖木兒及腹心之士孛倫赤、剌剌等議，以八月甲午昧爽，率勇士納只禿魯等入興聖宮，會集百官，執中書平章烏伯都剌、伯顏察兒，兵皆露刃，誓衆曰：「祖宗正統屬在武皇帝之子，敢有不順者斬。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he deliberated with Princess Chaqir, kinsman Alatimur, and trusted men such as Bolunchi and Lala. On the jiawu day of the eighth month at dawn, he led brave men including Nazhutulu into the Xingsheng Palace, assembled the hundred officials, seized Grand Councillors Ubdula and Bayancha'er, and with all troops baring blades swore to the multitude: "The orthodox succession of the ancestors belongs to the son of Emperor Wu; whoever dares disobey shall be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore conspired with Princess Chaqir, his kinsman Alatimur, and trusted followers Bolunchi and Lala. At dawn on the jiawu day of the eighth month he led warriors including Nazhutulu into the Xingsheng Palace, assembled the officials, seized Grand Councillors Ubdula and Bayancha'er, and with blades drawn swore to the assembly: "The legitimate succession belongs to Wuzong's son. Whoever resists will be executed."

sentences.zh: 衆皆潰散。

translations.literal: The multitude all scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd scattered in panic.

sentences.zh: 遂捕姦黨下獄，而與西安王阿剌忒納失里入守內庭，分處腹心於樞密，自東華門夾道重列軍士，使人傳命往來其中，以防漏泄。

translations.literal: He then arrested the treacherous faction and imprisoned them, and together with Prince of Xi'an Alatanashili entered to guard the inner court. He stationed trusted men at the Bureau of Military Affairs and lined soldiers in double ranks along the road from the Donghua Gate, sending men to convey orders back and forth among them to prevent leaks.
translations.idiomatic: He arrested the conspirators and imprisoned them, then entered the inner court with the Prince of Xi'an, Alatanashili, to hold it. He posted trusted men at the Bureau of Military Affairs and lined troops in double ranks from the Donghua Gate, sending messengers among them to prevent any leak of intelligence.

sentences.zh: 即命前河南行省參知政事明里董阿、前宣政院使荅剌麻失里乘驛迎文宗于中興，且令密以意喻河南行省平章伯顏選兵備扈從。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered the former Vice Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat Minglidong'a and the former Commissioner of the Xuanzheng Bureau Darlamashili to ride post-horses and welcome Wenzong from Zhongxing, and secretly instructed them to convey his intent to Bayan, Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, to select troops and prepare an escort.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately dispatched the former Vice Administrator of Henan, Minglidong'a, and the former Xuanzheng Commissioner Darlamashili by post-horse to welcome Wenzong from Zhongxing, and secretly instructed them to tell Bayan, Grand Councillor of Henan, to assemble troops for an escort.

sentences.zh: 於是封府庫，拘百司印，遣兵守諸要害。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sealed the treasuries, seized the seals of the hundred offices, and dispatched troops to guard all strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the treasuries, seized the seals of government offices, and posted troops at every strategic point.

sentences.zh: 推前湖廣行省左丞相別不花為中書左丞相，詹事塔失海涯為平章，前湖廣行省右丞速速為中書左丞，前陝西行省參政王不憐吉台為樞密副使，蕭忙古仍為通政院使，與中書右丞趙世延、樞密同僉燕鐵木兒、通政院使寒食分典庶務。

translations.literal: He promoted the former Left Grand Councillor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat Babuhua to Left Grand Councillor of the Secretariat; the Household Mentor Tashihaiya to Grand Councillor; the former Right Vice Administrator of Huguang Susu to Left Vice Administrator; the former Vice Administrator of Shaanxi Wangbulinjie to Deputy Administrator of Military Affairs; Xiao Manggu to Commissioner of the Bureau of Transmission; and together with Right Vice Administrator Zhao Shiyan, Associate Administrator of Military Affairs El Temür, and Commissioner of Transmission Hanshi, they divided administration of routine affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Babuhua, former Left Grand Councillor of Huguang, as Left Grand Councillor; Tashihaiya as Grand Councillor; Susu as Left Vice Administrator; Wangbulinjie as Deputy Administrator of Military Affairs; and Xiao Manggu as Commissioner of Transmission. Together with Zhao Shiyan, El Temür, and Hanshi, they divided the administration of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 貸在京寺觀鈔，募死士，買戰馬，運京倉粟以餉守禦士卒，復遣使於各行省徵發錢帛兵器。

translations.literal: He borrowed paper money from temples and monasteries in the capital, recruited dare-to-die men, purchased war horses, transported grain from the capital granaries to provision the defending troops, and again sent envoys to the branch secretariats to levy funds, silks, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He borrowed funds from capital temples and monasteries, recruited dare-to-die fighters, bought war horses, drew grain from the capital granaries to feed the garrison, and sent envoys to the provinces to levy money, silk, and arms.

sentences.zh: 當時有諸衛軍無統屬者，又有謁選及罷退軍官，皆給之符牌，以待調遣。

translations.literal: At that time there were guard units without command, and also officers who had presented themselves for selection and officers who had been dismissed or retired—all were given tally plaques to await deployment.
translations.idiomatic: Guard units without commanders, officers awaiting appointment, and dismissed officers were all issued tally plaques pending deployment.

sentences.zh: 既受命，未知所謝，注目而立，乃指使南向拜，衆皆愕然，始知有定向矣。

translations.literal: After receiving their orders, not knowing how to thank him, they stood gazing fixedly. He then directed them to bow facing south, and all were startled—only then did they know there was a fixed direction.
translations.idiomatic: When they received their orders they stood uncertain how to respond until he directed them to bow facing south. All were startled, for only then did they understand which prince they served.

sentences.zh: 燕鐵木兒宿衛禁中，夜則更遷無定居，坐以待旦者，將一月。

translations.literal: El Temür lodged on guard within the forbidden precincts; at night he shifted without fixed dwelling, sitting to await dawn—for nearly a month.
translations.idiomatic: El Temür kept watch inside the palace, changing his quarters each night and sitting awake until dawn—for nearly a month.

sentences.zh: 弟撒敦、子唐其勢時留上都，密遣塔失帖木兒召之，皆棄其妻子來歸。

translations.literal: His younger brother Sadun and his son Tangqishi were then detained at Shangdu. He secretly sent Tashitemur to summon them; both abandoned their wives and children and came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Sadun and son Tangqishi were still at Shangdu. He secretly sent Tashitemur to summon them, and both abandoned their families to join him.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，再遣撒里不花、鎖南班往中興趣大駕早發，令塔失帖木兒設為南使云：「諸王帖木兒不花、寬徹普化，湖廣、河南省臣及河南都萬戶合軍扈駕，旦夕且至，民勿疑懼。」

translations.literal: On the dingyou day he again sent Saribuhua and Suonanban to Zhongxing to urge the imperial carriage to depart early, and ordered Tashitemur to pose as a southern envoy, saying: "Princes Temurbuhua and Kunchepuhua, the Huguang and Henan provincial ministers, and the Commander-in-Chief of Henan are combining armies to escort the throne; they will arrive within days—let the people not doubt or fear."
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day he again sent Saribuhua and Suonanban to Zhongxing to hurry the imperial procession, and had Tashitemur pose as a southern envoy announcing that princes and provincial armies were escorting the throne and would arrive within days, so the people should not fear.

sentences.zh: 丁未，命撒敦以兵守居庸關，唐其勢屯古北口。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day he ordered Sadun to hold Juyong Pass with troops and Tangqishi to encamp at Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day he ordered Sadun to hold Juyong Pass and Tangqishi to encamp at Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 戊申，復令乃馬台為北使，稱明宗從諸王兵整駕南轅，中外乃安。

translations.literal: On the wushen day he again ordered Namatai as northern envoy, declaring that Mingzong was following the princes' troops in marshaling the carriage southward, and within and without were thereby reassured.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day he sent Namatai as northern envoy to announce that Mingzong was marching south with the princes' armies, calming court and country alike.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，撒里不花至自中興，云乘輿已啟塗，詔拜燕鐵木兒知樞密院事。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day Saribuhua arrived from Zhongxing, reporting that the imperial carriage had already set out on the road. An edict appointed El Temür Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day Saribuhua returned from Zhongxing with word that the imperial procession had set out. El Temür was appointed Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，率百官備法駕郊迎。

translations.literal: On the bingchen day he led the hundred officials with the full imperial equipage to welcome the emperor at the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day he led the officials out with the full imperial equipage to welcome the emperor.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，文宗至京師，入居大內。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day Wenzong reached the capital and entered residence in the great inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day Wenzong reached the capital and took up residence in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，封燕鐵木兒為太平王，以太平路為其食邑。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day El Temür was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiping, with Taiping Circuit as his fief.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day El Temür was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiping, with Taiping Circuit as his fief.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，加開府儀同三司、上柱國、錄軍國重事、中書右丞相、監修國史、知樞密院事；

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day he was further granted Commissioner with Credentials Equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar of State, Recorder of Weighty Affairs of Army and State, Right Grand Councillor of the Secretariat, Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History, and Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day he was further appointed Commissioner with Credentials Equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar of State, Recorder of Weighty Affairs of Army and State, Right Grand Councillor, Supervisor of the National History, and Administrator of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 賜黃金五百兩、白金二千五百兩、鈔一萬錠、金素織段色繒二千匹、海東白鶻一、青鶻二、豹一、平江官地五百頃。

translations.literal: He was granted five hundred liang of gold, two thousand five hundred liang of silver, ten thousand ingots of paper money, two thousand bolts of gold-thread and plain woven silks and colored silks, one eastern white gyrfalcon, two blue gyrfalcons, one leopard, and five hundred qing of official land in Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He received five hundred liang of gold, two thousand five hundred liang of silver, ten thousand ingots of paper money, two thousand bolts of silk, one white gyrfalcon, two blue gyrfalcons, a leopard, and five hundred qing of official land in Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 即日詔將兵出薊州拒禿滿迭兒。

translations.literal: That same day an edict ordered him to lead troops out from Jizhou to resist Tudmandar.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was ordered to lead troops from Jizhou against Tudmandar.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，次三河，而王禪等軍已破居庸關，遂進屯三塚。

translations.literal: On the yihai day he halted at Sanhe, while Wangchan's army had already broken through Juyong Pass; he therefore advanced and encamped at Sanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day he halted at Sanhe, but Wangchan's army had already broken through Juyong Pass, so he advanced and encamped at Sanzhong.

sentences.zh: 丙子，燕鐵木兒蓐食倍道而還。

translations.literal: On the bingzi day El Temür ate upon his mat and returned at double speed.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day El Temür ate on the march and raced back at double speed.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，抵榆河，聞帝出都城，將親督戰，燕鐵木兒單騎請見，曰：「陛下出，民心必驚，凡剪寇事一以責臣，願陛下亟還宮以安黎庶。」

translations.literal: On the dingchou day he reached the Yu River and heard that the emperor had left the capital and was about to command the battle in person. El Temür rode alone to request audience and said: "If Your Majesty goes out, the people's hearts will surely be alarmed. Let all matters of cutting down the bandits be charged entirely to your servant. I beg Your Majesty to return quickly to the palace to reassure the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day he reached the Yu River and learned that the emperor had left the capital to command the battle in person. El Temür rode alone to audience and said, "If Your Majesty goes out, the people will panic. Leave the campaign entirely to me and return to the palace at once to reassure them."

sentences.zh: 文宗乃還。

translations.literal: Wenzong thereupon returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong returned.

sentences.zh: 明日丁丑，阿速衛指揮使忽都不花、塔海帖木兒，同知太不花構變，事覺，械送京師斬以徇。

translations.literal: The next day, dingchou, the Asud Guard commanders Hudubuhua and Tahaitemur and Vice Administrator Taibuhua plotted rebellion; when the affair was discovered they were shackled, sent to the capital, and beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Asud Guard commanders Hudubuhua and Tahaitemur and Vice Administrator Taibuhua plotted mutiny. When discovered they were sent to the capital in chains and executed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 己卯，與王禪前軍遇于榆河北，我師奮擊敗之，追至紅橋北。

translations.literal: On the jimao day he encountered Wangchan's vanguard north of the Yu River; our army fought fiercely and defeated them, pursuing to north of Hong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day he met Wangchan's vanguard north of the Yu River, routed them in fierce fighting, and pursued to north of Hong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 王禪將樞密副使阿剌帖木兒、指揮忽都帖木兒引兵會戰。

translations.literal: Wangchan led Deputy Administrator of Military Affairs Alatimur and Commander Hudutemur to bring troops and join battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wangchan brought Deputy Administrator Alatimur and Commander Hudutemur to join the fight.

sentences.zh: 阿剌帖木兒執戈入刺，燕鐵木兒側身以刀格其戈就斫之，中左臂。

translations.literal: Alatimur grasped a halberd and thrust in to stab; El Temür turned aside and with his knife blocked the halberd and then hacked at him, striking the left arm.
translations.idiomatic: Alatimur thrust at him with a halberd. El Temür turned aside, parried with his sword, and struck, wounding Alatimur's left arm.

sentences.zh: 部將和尚馳擊忽都帖木兒亦中左臂。

translations.literal: His subordinate general Heshang galloped to strike Hudutemur and also hit the left arm.
translations.idiomatic: His officer Heshang charged Hudutemur and wounded his left arm as well.

sentences.zh: 二人驍將也，敵為奪氣，遂却。

translations.literal: The two were fierce generals; the enemy lost their spirit and therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Both were fierce warriors, and when they were wounded the enemy lost heart and fell back.

sentences.zh: 因據紅橋。

translations.literal: He thereupon held Hong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He then held Hong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 兩軍阻水而陣，命善射者射之，遂退，師于白浮南。

translations.literal: The two armies arrayed with the water between them; he ordered skilled archers to shoot, and the enemy then withdrew. He encamped south of Baifu.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies faced each other across the water. He ordered archers to shoot until the enemy withdrew, then encamped south of Baifu.

sentences.zh: 命知院也速荅兒，八都兒、亦納思等分為三隊，張兩翼以角之，敵軍敗走。

translations.literal: He ordered the administrators Yesuda'er, Badu'er, and Yinas to divide into three columns and spread two wings to corner them; the enemy army was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He divided his forces under Yesuda'er, Badu'er, and Yinas into three columns with wings to envelop the enemy, who broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，敵軍復合，鏖戰于白浮之野，周旋馳突，戈戟戞摩。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day the enemy army reassembled and fought a bitter battle on the plain of Baifu, wheeling and charging, halberds and spears clashing.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day the enemy reformed and fought a bitter battle on the Baifu plain, wheeling and charging as halberds clashed.

sentences.zh: 燕鐵木兒手斃七人。

translations.literal: El Temür with his own hand killed seven men.
translations.idiomatic: El Temür personally killed seven men.

sentences.zh: 會日晡，對壘而宿。

translations.literal: When the afternoon came, the two sides faced each other in camp and lodged for the night.
translations.idiomatic: By afternoon the two armies faced each other and camped for the night.

sentences.zh: 夜二鼓，遣阿剌帖木兒、孛倫赤、岳來吉將精銳百騎鼓譟射其營，敵衆驚擾，互自相擊，至旦始悟，人馬死傷無數。

translations.literal: At the second watch of the night he sent Alatimur, Bolunchi, and Yuelaiji to lead a hundred elite horsemen to beat drums, raise clamor, and shoot into their camp. The enemy multitude was alarmed and thrown into disorder, striking one another; only at dawn did they realize, and men and horses died and were wounded beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch he sent Alatimur, Bolunchi, and Yuelaiji with a hundred elite horsemen to raid the enemy camp with drums and arrows. The enemy panicked and attacked one another; only at dawn did they realize what had happened, with countless dead and wounded.

sentences.zh: 明日，天大霧，獲敵卒二人，云王禪等脫身竄山谷矣。

translations.literal: The next day there was heavy fog. They captured two enemy soldiers who said Wangchan and others had escaped into the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, in thick fog, they captured two enemy soldiers who reported that Wangchan and the others had fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 癸未，天清明，王禪集散卒成列出山，我師駐白浮西，堅壁不動。

translations.literal: On the guiwei day the sky cleared. Wangchan gathered scattered troops into ranks and came out from the mountains. Our army encamped west of Baifu and held the walls without moving.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day, with skies clear, Wangchan reformed his scattered troops and came out of the hills. El Temür's army held west of Baifu behind fortified lines and did not move.

sentences.zh: 是夜，又命撒敦潛軍繞其後，部曲八都兒壓其前，夾營吹銅角以震盪之，敵不悟而亂，自相撾擊，三鼓後乃西遁。

translations.literal: That night he again ordered Sadun to lead troops secretly around their rear while the detachment Badu'er pressed their front. From both sides of the camp they blew bronze horns to shake them. The enemy, not understanding, fell into disorder and struck one another; only after the third watch did they flee westward.
translations.idiomatic: That night he sent Sadun to circle behind the enemy while Badu'er pressed from the front. Horns blared from both sides of the camp. The enemy, confused, fell into disorder and attacked one another, fleeing westward only after the third watch.

sentences.zh: 遲明，追及昌平北，斬首數千級，降者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Near dawn they pursued as far as north of Changping, taking several thousand heads and receiving the surrender of more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Near dawn they pursued to north of Changping, taking several thousand heads and accepting the surrender of more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 帝遣賜上尊，諭旨曰：「丞相每戰親冒矢石，脫有不虞，其若宗社何！

translations.literal: The emperor sent a gift of fine wine and an instruction, saying: "The chief minister in every battle personally braves arrows and stones. If something untoward should occur, what of the altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent fine wine with a message: "In every battle you expose yourself to arrows and stones. If anything should befall you, what would become of the dynasty?

sentences.zh: 自今後但憑高督戰，察將士之用命不用命者以賞罰之可也。」

translations.literal: From now on you need only command the battle from high ground, observe which officers and soldiers obey orders and which do not, and reward and punish accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter command from high ground and reward or punish your officers according to their performance."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣以身先之，為諸將法。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant takes the lead with my body to set an example for the generals.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I lead from the front to set an example for my generals.

sentences.zh: 敢後者軍法從事。

translations.literal: Whoever dares lag behind will be dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever hangs back faces military law.

sentences.zh: 託之諸將，萬一失利，悔將何及。」

translations.literal: If entrusted to the generals, should there be the slightest defeat, what regret would suffice?"
translations.idiomatic: If I leave it to them and we lose, regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 是日，敵軍再戰再北，王禪單騎亡命。

translations.literal: That day the enemy army fought twice and was twice defeated; Wangchan fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: That day the enemy fought twice and was twice defeated. Wangchan fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 也速荅兒、也不倫、撒敦追之，就命也速荅兒及僉院徹里帖木兒統卒三萬守居庸關，還至昌平南。

translations.literal: Yesuda'er, Yebulun, and Sadun pursued him. He thereupon ordered Yesuda'er and Associate Administrator Cheritemur to command thirty thousand troops to hold Juyong Pass, and returned to south of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Yesuda'er, Yebulun, and Sadun pursued him. El Temür ordered Yesuda'er and Cheritemur to hold Juyong Pass with thirty thousand men and returned to south of Changping.

sentences.zh: 俄報古北口不守，上都軍掠石槽。

translations.literal: Soon it was reported that Gubeikou was not held and that the Shangdu army was plundering Shicao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Gubeikou had fallen and Shangdu troops were raiding Shicao.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，遣撒敦為先驅，燕鐵木兒以大軍繼其後，至石槽。

translations.literal: On the bingxu day he sent Sadun as vanguard; El Temür followed with the great army and reached Shicao.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day he sent Sadun ahead while El Temür followed with the main army to Shicao.

sentences.zh: 敵軍方炊，掩其不備，直蹂之，大軍并進，追擊四十里，至牛頭山，擒駙馬孛羅帖木兒，平章蒙古荅失、牙失帖木兒，院使撒兒討溫等，獻俘闕下，戮之。

translations.literal: The enemy army was just cooking; he surprised them unprepared and overran them directly. The great army advanced together, pursuing for forty li to Niutou Mountain. They captured the imperial son-in-law Boluotemur, Grand Councillor Monggol Dash, Yashitemur, and Commissioner Sarituwen, presented the captives below the palace, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy were cooking their meal when he fell on them unawares, overran them, and pursued forty li to Niutou Mountain. He captured the imperial son-in-law Boluotemur, Grand Councillor Monggol Dash, Yashitemur, and Commissioner Sarituwen, presented them at court, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 各衛將士降者不可勝紀，餘兵奔竄。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers of the various guards who surrendered were beyond counting; the remaining troops fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Countless guards surrendered; the rest fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 夜遣撒敦襲之，逐出古北口。

translations.literal: At night he sent Sadun to strike them and drive them out through Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: That night he sent Sadun to strike them and drive them out through Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，禿滿迭兒及諸王也先帖木兒軍陷通州，將襲京師，燕鐵木兒急引軍還。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day Tudmandar and the army of Prince Yexiantemur captured Tongzhou and were about to strike the capital. El Temür urgently led his army back.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day Tudmandar and Prince Yexiantemur's army took Tongzhou and threatened the capital. El Temür hurried back with his army.

sentences.zh: 十月己丑朔，日將昏，至通州，乘其初至擊之，敵軍狼狽走渡潞河。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month, jichou, as the sun was about to set, he reached Tongzhou and struck them as they had just arrived. The enemy army fled in disarray across the Lu River.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month, as dusk approached, he reached Tongzhou and struck the enemy as they were just arriving. They fled in disorder across the Lu River.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，夾河而軍。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day the two armies encamped on opposite banks of the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day the two armies encamped on opposite banks.

sentences.zh: 敵列植黍稭，衣以氊衣，然火為疑兵，夜遁。

translations.literal: The enemy planted millet stalks in rows, clothed them in felt garments, set fire to them as decoy troops, and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy planted millet stalks dressed in felt, set them ablaze as decoys, and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，率師渡河追之。

translations.literal: On the xinmao day he led his army across the river in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day he crossed the river in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，駐檀子山之棗林，也先帖木兒、禿滿迭兒合陽翟王太平、國王朶羅台、平章塔海軍來鬪，士皆殊死戰。

translations.literal: On the guisi day he encamped in the jujube grove of Tanzishan. Yexiantemur and Tudmandar combined with Prince Taiping of Yangzhai, Prince Duoluotai, and Grand Councillor Tahai's army to come and fight; the soldiers all fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day he encamped in the jujube grove at Tanzishan. Yexiantemur and Tudmandar joined Prince Taiping of Yangzhai, Prince Duoluotai, and Grand Councillor Tahai in battle. Both sides fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 至晚，唐其勢陷陣，殺太平，死者蔽野，餘兵宵潰。

translations.literal: By evening Tangqishi broke into the enemy formation and killed Taiping. The dead covered the field; the remaining troops fled in the night.
translations.idiomatic: By evening Tangqishi broke through the enemy line and killed Taiping. The dead covered the field and the survivors fled by night.

sentences.zh: 已而撒敦將輕兵要之，弗及而還。

translations.literal: Afterward Sadun led light troops to intercept them but did not overtake them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Sadun then led light troops to intercept them but failed to overtake them and returned.

sentences.zh: 乙未，上都諸王忽剌台，指揮阿剌鐵木兒、安童入紫荊關，犯良鄉，游騎逼南城。

translations.literal: On the yiwei day the Shangdu prince Hulatai and the commanders Alatimur and Antong entered Zijing Pass, invaded Liangxiang, and roaming horsemen pressed the southern city.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day the Shangdu prince Hulatai and commanders Alatimur and Antong entered Zijing Pass, raided Liangxiang, and scouting horsemen threatened the southern suburbs of the capital.

sentences.zh: 燕鐵木兒即率諸將兵循北山而西，令脫銜繫囊，盛莝豆以飼馬，士行且食，晨夜兼程，至于盧溝河，忽剌台聞之，望風西走。

translations.literal: El Temür immediately led the generals' troops along the northern mountains westward. He ordered them to remove bits and tie bags, fill them with chopped beans to feed the horses, and let the soldiers eat as they marched day and night without rest until they reached the Lugou River. When Hulatai heard of this, he fled west at the sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: El Temür immediately led his generals west along the northern hills. He had the troops remove bits, fill saddlebags with chopped fodder, and march day and night eating on the move until they reached the Lugou River. Hulatai fled west at the news.

sentences.zh: 是日凱旋，入自肅清門，都人羅拜馬首，以謝更生之惠。

translations.literal: That day he returned in triumph, entering by the Suqing Gate. The people of the capital lined up to bow at his horse's head, thanking him for the grace of renewed life.
translations.idiomatic: That day he returned in triumph through the Suqing Gate. The people lined the streets to bow before his horse, thanking him for saving their lives.

sentences.zh: 燕鐵木兒曰：「此皆天子威靈，吾何力焉。」

translations.literal: El Temür said: "This is all the Son of Heaven's august power—what strength is mine?"
translations.idiomatic: El Temür said, "This is all the emperor's majesty—what credit is mine?"

sentences.zh: 入見，帝大悅，賜燕興聖殿，盡懽而罷。

translations.literal: He entered audience; the emperor was greatly pleased, granted a banquet in the Xingsheng Hall, and they enjoyed themselves fully before dispersing.
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor was overjoyed, gave a banquet in the Xingsheng Hall, and they feasted until all dispersed.

sentences.zh: 賜太平王黃金印，并降制書及賜玉盤、龍衣、珠衣、寶珠、金腰帶等物。

translations.literal: He was granted the Prince of Taiping's golden seal, and an imperial patent was issued together with gifts of jade platters, dragon robes, pearl robes, precious pearls, golden belts, and other objects.
translations.idiomatic: He received the Prince of Taiping's golden seal, an imperial patent, and gifts including jade platters, dragon robes, pearl robes, precious pearls, and golden belts.

sentences.zh: 是日，撒敦遣報禿滿迭兒軍復入古北口，燕鐵木兒遂以師赴之，戰于檀州南野，敗之。

translations.literal: That day Sadun sent word that Tudmandar's army had again entered Gubeikou. El Temür thereupon led his army to meet them, fought on the southern plain of Tanzhou, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Sadun reported that Tudmandar's army had re-entered Gubeikou. El Temür marched against them, fought on the southern plain of Tanzhou, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 東路蒙古萬戶哈剌那懷率麾下萬人降，餘兵東潰，禿滿迭兒走還遼東。

translations.literal: The Eastern Route Mongol commander-in-chief Qalanaqai led his ten thousand men under his command to surrender; the remaining troops fled east in rout, and Tudmandar fled back to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Route Mongol commander Qalanaqai surrendered with ten thousand men. The rest fled east and Tudmandar retreated to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 獲忽剌台、阿剌帖木兒、安童、朶羅台、塔海等戮之。

translations.literal: They captured Hulatai, Alatimur, Antong, Duoluotai, Tahai, and others and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Hulatai, Alatimur, Antong, Duoluotai, Tahai, and others were captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 先是，至治二年，以欽察衛士多，為千戶所者凡三十五，故分置左右二衛，至是又析為龍翊衛。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the second year of Zhizhi, because there were many Qipchaq guards, there were thirty-five thousand-household offices; therefore left and right guards were separately established. At this time they were further divided into the Longyi Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in 1322, because the Qipchaq guard was large—thirty-five thousand-household units—it had been split into left and right guards. Now it was further divided into the Longyi Guard.

sentences.zh: 二年，立都督府，以統左、右欽察、龍翊三衛，哈剌魯東路蒙古二萬戶府，東路蒙古元帥府，而以燕鐵木兒兼統之，尋陞為大都督府。

translations.literal: In the second year a command headquarters was established to oversee the left, right, and Longyi Qipchaq guards, the Eastern Route Qarluq Mongol two-ten-thousand-household office, and the Eastern Route Mongol marshal's headquarters, with El Temür concurrently commanding them; soon it was promoted to the Great Command Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year a command headquarters was established over the left, right, and Longyi Qipchaq guards and the eastern Mongol commands, with El Temür in overall command; it was soon elevated to the Great Command Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 燕鐵木兒乞解相印還宿衛，帝勉之曰：「卿已為省院，惟未入臺，其聽後命。」

translations.literal: El Temür requested to resign the chief minister's seal and return to palace guard duty. The emperor urged him: "You already serve the Secretariat and the Bureau; only you have not yet entered the Censorate—await further orders."
translations.idiomatic: El Temür asked to resign the chief minister's seal and return to palace guard duty. The emperor urged him, "You already head the Secretariat and the Bureau; only the Censorate remains—await further orders."

sentences.zh: 二月，遷御史大夫，依前開府儀同三司、上柱國、錄軍國重事、太平王。

translations.literal: In the second month he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief, retaining his former titles as Commissioner with Credentials Equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar of State, Recorder of Weighty Affairs of Army and State, and Prince of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was made Censor-in-Chief while retaining his titles as Commissioner with Credentials Equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar of State, Recorder of Weighty Affairs, and Prince of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復拜中書右丞相、監修國史、知樞密院事、領都督府龍翊侍衛親軍都指揮使司事，就佩元降虎符，依前開府儀同三司、上柱國、錄軍國重事、荅剌罕、太平王。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Right Grand Councillor of the Secretariat, Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History, Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Director of the Command Headquarters' Longyi Palace Guard Elite Army Command, wearing on the spot the tiger tally previously granted, and retaining his former titles as Commissioner with Credentials Equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar of State, Recorder of Weighty Affairs, Darqan, and Prince of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again appointed Right Grand Councillor, Supervisor of the National History, Administrator of Military Affairs, and commander of the Longyi Guard, wearing the tiger tally previously granted and retaining all his former honors including Darqan and Prince of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁亥，文宗以燕鐵木兒有大勳勞于王室，封其曾祖父班都察溧陽王，曾祖妣玉龍徹溧陽王夫人，祖父土土哈昇王，祖妣太塔你昇王夫人，父床兀兒揚王，母也先帖你、公主察吉兒並為揚王夫人。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day of the twelfth month, because El Temür had great meritorious service to the royal house, Wenzong enfeoffed his great-grandfather Banducha as Prince of Liyang, his great-grandmother Yulongche as Lady of the Prince of Liyang, his grandfather Tutuqa as Prince Sheng, his grandmother Tatai as Lady of Prince Sheng, his father Chen'er as Prince Yang, and his mother Yexianteni and Princess Chaqir both as Ladies of the Prince of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the twelfth month Wenzong, honoring El Temür's great service to the dynasty, enfeoffed his ancestors: great-grandfather Banducha as Prince of Liyang, great-grandmother Yulongche as his consort, grandfather Tutuqa as Prince Sheng, grandmother Tatai as his consort, father Chen'er as Prince Yang, and mother Yexianteni and Princess Chaqir as Ladies of Prince Yang.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，文宗欲昭其勳，詔命禮部尚書馬祖常制文立石於北郊。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year Wenzong wished to proclaim his merit and ordered Minister of Rites Ma Zuchang to compose a text and erect a stone at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year Wenzong wished to commemorate his merit and ordered Minister of Rites Ma Zuchang to compose an inscription and erect a stele at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 至順元年五月乙丑，帝又以屢頒寵數未足以報大勳，下詔命獨為丞相以尊異之。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of the fifth month of the first year of Zhishun, the emperor, considering that repeated bestowals of favor were still insufficient to repay his great merit, issued an edict appointing him sole chief minister to honor him exceptionally.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the fifth month of the first year of Zhishun the emperor, judging repeated honors insufficient to repay his great service, issued an edict making him sole chief minister in exceptional recognition.

sentences.zh: 略曰：「燕鐵木兒勳勞惟舊，忠勇多謀，奮大義以成功，致治平於期月，宜專獨運，以重秉鈞。

translations.literal: In summary it said: "El Temür's meritorious toil is of long standing; he is loyal, brave, and full of stratagems. He roused great righteousness to achieve success and brought orderly rule within a month's time. He ought to wield sole authority to bear heavily the scales of state.
translations.idiomatic: It read in part: "El Temür's service is of long standing; he is loyal, brave, and resourceful. He upheld righteousness to victory and brought order within a month. He should wield sole authority as the pivot of state.

sentences.zh: 授以開府儀同三司、上柱國、太師、太平王、荅剌罕、中書右丞相、錄軍國重事、監修國史、提調燕王宮相府事、大都督、領龍翊親軍都指揮使司事。

translations.literal: He was granted Commissioner with Credentials Equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar of State, Grand Preceptor, Prince of Taiping, Darqan, Right Grand Councillor of the Secretariat, Recorder of Weighty Affairs of Army and State, Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History, Supervisor of the Prince of Yan's Palace Chancellor's Office, Great Commander, and Director of the Longyi Elite Army Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted Commissioner with Credentials Equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar of State, Grand Preceptor, Prince of Taiping, Darqan, Right Grand Councillor, Recorder of Weighty Affairs, Supervisor of the National History, Supervisor of the Prince of Yan's household, Great Commander, and commander of the Longyi Guard.

sentences.zh: 凡號令、刑名、選法、錢糧、造作，一切中書政務，悉聽緫裁。

translations.literal: All orders, penal names, selection law, funds and grain, and construction—all Secretariat affairs—were entirely subject to his overall adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: All orders, law, appointments, revenue, and construction—in short, all Secretariat affairs—were placed entirely under his authority.

sentences.zh: 諸王、公主、駙馬、近侍人員，大小諸衙門官員人等，敢有隔越聞奏，以違制論。」

translations.literal: Imperial princes, princesses, imperial sons-in-law, close attendants, and officials great and small of all yamen—whoever dared to bypass him in memorializing would be judged under the statute for violating regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes, princesses, sons-in-law, attendants, and officials of every office who bypassed him in memorializing would be punished for violating regulations."

sentences.zh: 六月，知樞密院事闊徹伯、脫脫木兒等十人惡其權勢之重，欲謀害之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the administrators of military affairs Kuochebo, Tuotuomur, and ten others resented the weight of his power and wished to plot his murder.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Kuochebo, Tuotuomur, and ten others, resenting his overwhelming power, plotted to kill him.

sentences.zh: 也的迷失、脫迷以其謀告燕鐵木兒，即率欽察軍掩捕按問，皆誅之。

translations.literal: Yademishi and Tuomi reported their plot to El Temür. He immediately led Qipchaq troops to seize them in a surprise arrest and interrogate them; all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yademishi and Tuomi revealed the plot to El Temür, who immediately led Qipchaq troops to arrest and interrogate them. All were executed.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，為建第於興聖宮之西南。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year a residence was built for him southwest of the Xingsheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year a residence was built for him southwest of the Xingsheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 三月，賜鷹坊百人。

translations.literal: In the third month he was granted a hundred men from the hawkery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was granted a hundred men from the imperial falconry.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸未，詔養其子塔剌海為子。

translations.literal: On the guiwei day of the eleventh month an edict ordered that his son Talahai be adopted as the emperor's son.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day of the eleventh month an edict ordered that his son Talahai be adopted as the emperor's son.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以燕鐵木兒兼奎章閣大學士，領奎章閣學士院事。

translations.literal: On the xinyou day El Temür was additionally appointed Grand Academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion and was put in charge of the affairs of the Kui Zhang Pavilion Academy.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day El Temür was additionally made Grand Academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion and placed in charge of its academy.

sentences.zh: 賜龍慶州之流盃園池水磑土田。

translations.literal: He was granted the Liubei Garden, pool, watermill, and fields and land in Longqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the Liubei Garden, its pool and watermill, and adjoining fields in Longqing Prefecture.
