sentences.zh: 又賜平江、松江、江陰蘆場、簜山、沙塗、沙田等地。

translations.literal: He was further granted reed marshes, Daishan, sand flats, tidal fields, and other lands in Pingjiang, Songjiang, and Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted reed marshes, Daishan, sand flats, tidal fields, and other lands in Pingjiang, Songjiang, and Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 因言平江、松江圩田五百頃有奇，糧七千七百石，願增為萬石入官，以所得餘米贍弟撒敦，詔從之。

translations.literal: He thereupon reported that the polder fields of Pingjiang and Songjiang amounted to more than five hundred qing, yielding seven thousand seven hundred shi of grain, and expressed the wish to increase the yield submitted to the state to ten thousand shi and use the surplus grain obtained thereby to support his younger brother Sadun. An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that the polder fields of Pingjiang and Songjiang totaled more than five hundred qing and yielded seven thousand seven hundred shi of grain. He asked to raise the official quota to ten thousand shi and use the surplus to support his brother Sadun. The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 是時，撒敦已死，唐其勢為中書左丞相，伯顏獨用事。

translations.literal: At this time Sadun was already dead. Tangqishi was Left Grand Councillor of the Secretariat, and Bayan alone wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: By then Sadun was dead. Tangqishi served as Left Grand Councillor, while Bayan alone held real power.

sentences.zh: 唐其勢忿曰：「天下本我家天下也，伯顏何人而位居吾上。」

translations.literal: Tangqishi said in anger: "The realm was originally the realm of our house—what sort of man is Bayan that he should stand above me?"
translations.idiomatic: Tangqishi fumed, "The empire belongs to our family. Who is Bayan to rank above me?"

sentences.zh: 遂與撒敦弟荅里潛蓄異心，交通所親諸王晃火帖木兒，謀援立以危社稷。

translations.literal: He thereupon secretly harbored disloyal intent together with Sadun's younger brother Dali, maintained contact with the prince he favored, Huohuotimur, and plotted to install him by force so as to endanger the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly plotted with Sadun's brother Dali, colluded with Prince Huohuotimur, and schemed to put the prince on the throne and overthrow the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 帝數召荅里不至。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly summoned Dali, but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Dali repeatedly, but he refused to appear.

sentences.zh: 郯王徹徹禿遂發其謀。

translations.literal: The Prince of Tan, Chechetu, thereupon exposed their plot.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tan, Chechetu, then exposed the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 六月三十日，唐其勢伏兵東郊，身率勇士突入宮闕。

translations.literal: On the thirtieth day of the sixth month Tangqishi hid troops in the eastern suburbs and personally led brave warriors in a sudden assault on the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirtieth day of the sixth month Tangqishi concealed troops in the eastern suburbs and personally led warriors in a surprise attack on the palace.

sentences.zh: 伯顏及完者帖木兒、定住、闊里吉思等掩捕獲之。

translations.literal: Bayan, together with Ojar Timur, Dingzhu, Koroghos, and others, launched a surprise arrest and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan, Ojar Timur, Dingzhu, Koroghos, and others seized him in a surprise raid.

sentences.zh: 唐其勢及其弟塔剌海皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Tangqishi and his younger brother Talahai were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: Tangqishi and his brother Talahai were both executed.

sentences.zh: 而其黨北奔荅里所，荅里即應以兵，殺使者哈兒哈倫、阿魯灰用以禡旗。

translations.literal: His partisans fled north to Dali's place, and Dali immediately responded with troops, killing the envoys Qarqaqan and Aruqai and using them to consecrate the battle standard.
translations.idiomatic: His followers fled north to Dali, who immediately took up arms, killed the envoys Qarqaqan and Aruqai, and used their blood to consecrate his battle standard.

sentences.zh: 帝遣阿弼諭之，又殺阿弼，而率其黨和尚、剌剌等逆戰，為搠思監、火兒灰、哈剌那海等所敗，遂奔晃火帖木兒。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Aibi to instruct him, but he killed Aibi as well, then led his partisans Heshang, Lala, and others to fight in opposition. They were defeated by Suosijian, Huo'erhui, Qalanaqai, and others, and he then fled to Huohuotimur.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Aibi to reason with him, but Dali killed Aibi too, then led his followers Heshang, Lala, and others into battle. Suosijian, Huo'erhui, Qalanaqai, and others defeated them, and he fled to Huohuotimur.

sentences.zh: 命孛羅、晃火兒不花追襲之，力窮勢促，阿魯渾察執荅里等送上都戮之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Boluo and Huohu'erbuqa to pursue and attack them. When their strength was exhausted and their situation desperate, Aruqunqa seized Dali and the others and sent them to Shangdu, where they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Boluo and Huohu'erbuqa were ordered to pursue them. When Dali's forces were spent, Aruqunqa captured him and his companions and sent them to Shangdu for execution.

sentences.zh: 晃火帖木兒自殺。

translations.literal: Huohuotimur killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huohuotimur took his own life.

sentences.zh: 怯薛官阿察赤亦預唐其勢之謀，欲殺伯顏，後擒付有司，具伏其辜，伏誅。

translations.literal: The kesig officer Achzhi also took part in Tangqishi's plot and wished to kill Bayan. Later he was captured and handed over to the authorities, fully confessed his crime, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The kesig officer Achzhi had also joined Tangqishi's plot and planned to kill Bayan. He was later captured, confessed fully, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 初，唐其勢事敗被擒，攀折殿檻不肯出。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tangqishi's affair failed and he was captured, he clung to and broke the hall balustrades and refused to come out.
translations.idiomatic: When Tangqishi's coup failed and he was seized, he clung to the hall balustrades, breaking them, and refused to be dragged out.

sentences.zh: 塔剌海走匿皇后坐下，后蔽之以衣，左右曳出斬之，血濺后衣。

translations.literal: Talahai fled and hid beneath the empress's seat. The empress screened him with her robe, but attendants dragged him out and beheaded him, and blood splashed the empress's garments.
translations.idiomatic: Talahai fled and hid under the empress's seat. She covered him with her robe, but attendants dragged him out and beheaded him, splashing blood on her clothing.

sentences.zh: 伯顏奏曰：「豈有兄弟為逆而皇后黨之者！」

translations.literal: Bayan memorialized, saying: "How can there be brothers who rebel, yet the empress shields them!"
translations.idiomatic: Bayan memorialized, "How can the empress shield rebels who are her own brothers?"

sentences.zh: 并執后。

translations.literal: He also had the empress seized.
translations.idiomatic: He had the empress arrested as well.

sentences.zh: 后呼帝曰：「陛下救我。」

translations.literal: The empress called to the emperor: "Your Majesty, save me."
translations.idiomatic: The empress cried to the emperor, "Your Majesty, save me!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝兄弟為逆，豈能相救邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your brothers committed treason—how could I save you!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Your brothers rebelled. How can I save you?"

sentences.zh: 乃遷皇后出宮，尋酖之于開平民舍，遂簿錄唐其勢家。

translations.literal: He thereupon removed the empress from the palace, and soon had her poisoned in a commoner's dwelling at Kaiping. He then inventoried the household of Tangqishi.
translations.idiomatic: He removed the empress from the palace and soon had her poisoned in a commoner's house at Kaiping, then seized and inventoried Tangqishi's estate.

sentences.zh: 伯颜，蔑兒吉䚟氏。

translations.literal: Bayan was of the Merkit clan.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan was a Merkit.

sentences.zh: 曾大父探馬哈兒，給事宿衛。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Tanqadar served in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Tanqadar served in the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 大父稱海，從憲宗伐宋，歿於王事。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chenghai followed Möngke in the campaign against Song and died in the service of the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chenghai followed Möngke's campaign against Song and died in the emperor's service.

sentences.zh: 父謹只兒，緫宿衛隆福太后宮。

translations.literal: His father Jinzhir commanded the palace guard of Empress Dowager Longfu's palace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jinzhir commanded the guard of Empress Dowager Longfu's palace.

sentences.zh: 伯顏弘毅深沉，明達果斷。

translations.literal: Bayan was magnanimous, resolute, deep, and sober; clear-sighted, decisive, and firm.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan was resolute and deep-minded, clear-sighted and decisive.

sentences.zh: 年十五，奉成宗命侍武宗于藩邸。

translations.literal: At the age of fifteen, by Chengzong's command he attended Wuzong at the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he was ordered by Chengzong to attend Prince Wuzong at his residence.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，從北征海都。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade he followed the northern campaign against Haidu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1299 he joined the northern campaign against Haidu.

sentences.zh: 五年，從至迭怯里古之地，力戰，又至哈剌塔之地，累捷，功為諸將先。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed the army to the place called Diekeligu and fought fiercely; he also reached the place called Qalata and repeatedly won victories, his merit ranking first among the generals.
translations.idiomatic: In 1301 he fought fiercely at Diekeligu and again at Qalata, winning repeated victories and ranking first among the generals in merit.

sentences.zh: 十年，斡羅思、失班等逃奔察八兒之地，武宗命伯顏追降之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Oros, Shiban, and others fled to the territory of Chabar. Wuzong ordered Bayan to pursue and induce their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In 1306, when Oros, Shiban, and others fled to Chabar's territory, Wuzong ordered Bayan to pursue them and accept their surrender.

sentences.zh: 十一年，武宗大會諸王駙馬於和林，錫號曰伯顏拔都兒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Wuzong held a great assembly of princes and imperial sons-in-law at Karakorum and granted him the title Bayan Bagatur.
translations.idiomatic: In 1307 Wuzong held a great assembly of princes and sons-in-law at Karakorum and granted him the title Bayan Bagatur.

sentences.zh: 致和元年七月，泰定帝崩。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Zhihe Emperor Taiding died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 1328 Emperor Taiding died.

sentences.zh: 八月，丞相燕鐵木兒遣明里董阿迎立武宗子懷王於江陵，道過河南，使以謀密告伯顏。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Chief Councillor El Temür dispatched Minglidong'a to welcome and install Wuzong's son Prince Huai at Jiangling. Passing through Henan, he had the plan secretly reported to Bayan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Chief Councillor El Temür sent Minglidong'a to welcome Wuzong's son Prince Huai at Jiangling and, passing through Henan, secretly informed Bayan of the plan.

sentences.zh: 伯顏嘆曰：「此吾君之子也。

translations.literal: Bayan sighed and said: "This is the son of my lord.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan sighed, "This is my lord's son.

sentences.zh: 吾夙荷武皇厚恩，委以心膂，今爵位至此，非覬萬一為己富貴計，大義所臨，曷敢顧望。」

translations.literal: I have long owed Wuzong a deep debt of grace and was entrusted as his heart and backbone. Now that my rank and office have reached this point, it is not that I covet the slightest advantage for my own wealth and honor; when great righteousness confronts me, how dare I hesitate and look back?"
translations.idiomatic: I have long owed Wuzong a deep debt and was trusted as one of his closest men. My rank is high, but I do not seek the smallest gain for myself. When duty calls, how can I hold back?"

sentences.zh: 即集僚屬明告以故。

translations.literal: He immediately assembled his subordinates and clearly told them the reason.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately assembled his staff and explained the situation plainly.

sentences.zh: 於是會計倉廩、府庫、穀粟、金帛之數，乘輿供御、牢餼膳羞、徒旅委積、士馬芻糒供億之須，以及賞賚犒勞之用，靡不備至。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reckoned the numbers of granaries, treasuries, grain, and gold and silk; the needs of the imperial carriage's supplies, sacrificial offerings and feast dishes, accumulated baggage trains, fodder and grain for troops and horses, and rewards and consolation payments—nothing was left unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: He then took stock of granaries, treasuries, grain, gold, and silk; calculated supplies for the imperial journey, ritual offerings, provisions for troops and horses, and funds for rewards and consolation—and prepared everything without exception.

sentences.zh: 不足，則檄州縣募民折輸明年田租，及貸商人貨貲，約倍息以償。

translations.literal: Where this was insufficient, he issued orders to the prefectures and counties to levy the people and collect next year's field rent in advance, and to borrow merchants' goods and capital, agreeing to repay at double interest.
translations.idiomatic: Where funds still fell short, he ordered the prefectures and counties to advance next year's land tax from the people and to borrow from merchants, promising repayment at double interest.

sentences.zh: 又不足，則邀東南常賦之經河南者，輒止之以給其費。

translations.literal: Where it was still insufficient, he intercepted the regular tribute from the southeast passing through Henan and stopped it to meet the expenses.
translations.idiomatic: If that was still not enough, he intercepted the regular tribute shipments from the southeast passing through Henan and diverted them to cover the costs.

sentences.zh: 徵發民丁，增置驛馬，補城櫓，浚濠池，修戰守之具，嚴徼邏斥堠，日被堅執銳，與僚佐曹掾籌其便宜。

translations.literal: He conscripted civilian laborers, added post horses, repaired battlements, dredged moats, prepared equipment for offense and defense, tightened patrols and outpost beacons, and day after day wore armor and grasped sharp weapons while discussing advantageous measures with his staff clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He conscripted laborers, added post horses, repaired walls and moats, prepared weapons of war, tightened patrols and outposts, and day after day wore armor while conferring with his staff on strategy.

sentences.zh: 即遣蒙哥不花以其事馳告懷王。

translations.literal: He immediately dispatched Mengkebuhua to ride post-horses and report the matter to Prince Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent Mengkebuhua by post-horse to inform Prince Huai.

sentences.zh: 又使羅里報燕鐵木兒曰：「公盡力京師，河南事我當自效。」

translations.literal: He also sent Luoli to report to El Temür: "Your Excellency exert yourself fully at the capital; as for Henan affairs, I shall serve on my own account."
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Luoli to tell El Temür, "Do your utmost at the capital—I will handle Henan myself."

sentences.zh: 伯顏別募勇士五千人以迎帝于南，而躬勒兵以俟。

translations.literal: Bayan separately recruited five thousand brave warriors to welcome the emperor from the south, while he personally marshaled troops and waited.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan separately recruited five thousand warriors to welcome the emperor from the south and personally took command to await his arrival.

sentences.zh: 參政脫別台曰：「今蒙古軍馬與宿衛之士皆在上都，而令探馬赤軍守諸隘，吾恐此事之不可成也。

translations.literal: Vice Administrator Tobetai said: "Now the Mongol armies and horses and the palace guard troops are all at Shangdu, while the tamachi troops hold the passes. I fear this affair cannot succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Administrator Tobetai said, "The Mongol armies and palace guards are all at Shangdu, and tamachi troops hold the passes. I fear this cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 我等圖保性命，他何計哉？」

translations.literal: Let us think only of preserving our lives—what other plan is there?"
translations.idiomatic: We should think only of saving our own lives. What other plan is there?"

sentences.zh: 伯顏不從其言。

translations.literal: Bayan did not follow his words.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 其夜，脫別台手刃欲殺伯顏為變，伯顏覺，遂拔劍殺之，奪其所部軍器，收馬千二百騎。

translations.literal: That night Tobetai drew his blade and tried to kill Bayan in a mutiny. Bayan became aware of it, drew his sword and killed him, seized the weapons of his command, and collected twelve hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: That night Tobetai tried to kill Bayan in a mutiny. Bayan detected the attempt, drew his sword and killed him, seized his troops' weapons, and took twelve hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 懷王命撒里不花拜伯顏河南行省左丞相。

translations.literal: Prince Huai ordered Saribuhua to appoint Bayan Left Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai had Saribuhua appoint Bayan Left Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 懷王至河南，伯顏屬櫜鞬，擐甲冑，與百官父老導入，咸俯伏稱萬歲，即上前叩頭勸進。

translations.literal: When Prince Huai reached Henan, Bayan wore bow case and quiver, donned armor and helmet, and together with officials and elders led him in. All prostrated themselves and shouted "Ten thousand years!" He then stepped forward, kowtowed, and urged him to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Huai reached Henan, Bayan wore bow case and quiver and full armor, and with officials and local elders escorted him in. All prostrated themselves and shouted their homage. Bayan then stepped forward, kowtowed, and urged the prince to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 懷王解金鎧、御服、寶刀及海東白鶻、文豹賜伯顏。

translations.literal: Prince Huai removed his golden armor, imperial robes, precious saber, eastern-sea white gyrfalcon, and patterned leopard and bestowed them on Bayan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai gave Bayan his golden armor, imperial robes, precious saber, an eastern-sea white gyrfalcon, and a patterned leopard.

sentences.zh: 明日扈從北行。

translations.literal: The next day he escorted him northward.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he escorted the prince north.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，順帝至自南服，入踐大位，嘉伯顏翊戴之功，拜中書右丞相、上柱國、監修國史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year Emperor Shun arrived from the southern regions and ascended the great throne. Honoring Bayan's merit in supporting and installing him, he appointed him Right Grand Councillor of the Secretariat, Upper Pillar of State, and Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year Emperor Shun returned from the south and took the throne. Honoring Bayan's role in installing him, he appointed him Right Grand Councillor, Upper Pillar of State, and Supervisor of the National History.

sentences.zh: 元統二年，進太師、奎章閣大學士，領太史院，兼領司天監、威武、阿速諸衛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong he was promoted to Grand Preceptor and Grand Academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion, directed the Bureau of Astronomy, and concurrently directed the Directorate of Astronomy and the Uwei and Asud guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuantong he was made Grand Preceptor and Grand Academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion, placed in charge of the Bureau of Astronomy, and given concurrent command of the Directorate of Astronomy and the Uwei and Asud guards.

sentences.zh: 奏復經筵，加知經筵事。

translations.literal: He memorialized for the restoration of the Classics Lectern and was additionally made Administrator of Classics Lectern Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to restore the imperial lecture series and was made its administrator.

sentences.zh: 十一月，進封秦王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 繼領太禧宗禋院、中政院、宣政院、隆祥使司、宮相諸內府，緫領蒙古、欽察、斡羅思諸衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: He successively directed the Bureau of Imperial Sacrifices, the Central Administration Bureau, the Xuanzheng Bureau, the Longxiang Commission, and the various inner palace chancelleries, and overall commanded the Mongol, Qipchaq, and Oros elite army commands.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to direct the Bureau of Imperial Sacrifices, the Central Administration Bureau, the Xuanzheng Bureau, the Longxiang Commission, and other inner palace offices, and to command the Mongol, Qipchaq, and Oros guards.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，唐其勢及其弟塔剌海私蓄異志，謀危社稷，伯顏奉詔誅之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year Tangqishi and his younger brother Talahai secretly harbored disloyal intent and plotted to endanger the altars of state. Bayan received an edict and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year Tangqishi and his brother Talahai secretly plotted against the dynasty. Bayan received orders and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 餘黨稱兵，又親率師往上都，擊破其衆。

translations.literal: The remaining partisans raised troops, and he again personally led an army to Shangdu and routed their forces.
translations.idiomatic: When the remaining rebels took up arms, he personally led troops to Shangdu and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 七月，伯顏鴆殺皇后伯牙吾氏，為匿唐其勢、塔剌海于后宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Bayan poisoned Empress Bayiyu because she had hidden Tangqishi and Talahai in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Bayan poisoned Empress Bayiyu for sheltering Tangqishi and Talahai in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 伯顏怒曰：「豈有兄弟謀不軌而姊妹黨之者乎！」

translations.literal: Bayan said in anger: "How can there be brothers who plot treason, yet a sister who shields them!"
translations.idiomatic: Bayan raged, "How can a sister shield brothers who plot treason!"

sentences.zh: 遂鴆之。

translations.literal: He thereupon poisoned her.
translations.idiomatic: He had her poisoned.

sentences.zh: 詔諭天下，用國初故事，賜伯顏以荅剌罕之號，俾世襲之。

translations.literal: An edict was proclaimed throughout the realm. Following the precedent of the founding of the dynasty, Bayan was granted the title of Darqan, to be inherited in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued throughout the realm. Following the founding precedent, Bayan was granted the title Darqan as a hereditary honor.

sentences.zh: 然伯顏自誅唐其勢之後，獨秉國鈞，專權自恣，變亂祖宗成憲，虐害天下，漸有姦謀。

translations.literal: Yet after Bayan executed Tangqishi he alone held the scales of state, wielded power arbitrarily, altered and disrupted the established statutes of the ancestors, tyrannized and harmed the realm, and gradually harbored treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: After executing Tangqishi, however, Bayan alone held the reins of power. He ruled arbitrarily, overturned ancestral institutions, oppressed the realm, and gradually turned to treacherous designs.

sentences.zh: 帝患之。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew alarmed.

sentences.zh: 初，伯顏欲以其姪脫脫宿衛，伺帝起居，懼涉物議，乃以樞密知院汪家奴、翰林承旨沙剌班同侍禁近，實屬意脫脫。

translations.literal: At first Bayan wished to have his nephew Toqto'a serve in the palace guard and watch the emperor's daily movements, but fearing public criticism he had the Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wangjianu and the Hanlin Academician Recipient Shaban attend together at the forbidden inner quarters, while in fact his intent rested on Toqto'a.
translations.idiomatic: At first Bayan wanted his nephew Toqto'a in the palace guard to watch the emperor's movements, but fearing criticism he posted Wangjianu and Shaban at court while placing his real trust in Toqto'a.

sentences.zh: 故脫脫政令日修而衛士拱聽約束。

translations.literal: Therefore Toqto'a's orders grew daily more strict, and the guards stood with folded hands listening to his commands.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a's authority grew daily, and the guards obeyed him without question.

sentences.zh: 伯顏自領諸衛精兵，以燕者不花為屏蔽，導從之盛，填溢街衢。

translations.literal: Bayan personally led the elite troops of the various guards, with Yanzhebuhua as his screen. The splendor of his escort filled and overflowed the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan personally commanded elite guard troops, with Yanzhebuhua as his shield. His escort filled the streets.

sentences.zh: 而帝側儀衛反落落如晨星。

translations.literal: Yet the ceremonial guard at the emperor's side was instead sparse as the morning stars.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's own guard, by contrast, was sparse as morning stars.

sentences.zh: 勢燄薰灼，天下之人惟知有伯顏而已。

translations.literal: His power and flame scorched all around; the people of the realm knew only Bayan.
translations.idiomatic: His power blazed so fiercely that the people knew no authority but Bayan's.

sentences.zh: 脫脫深憂之，乘間自陳忘家徇國之意，帝猶未之信。

translations.literal: Toqto'a was deeply troubled by this. Seizing an opportunity, he declared himself willing to forget family and devote himself to the state, but the emperor still did not yet believe him.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a was deeply troubled. He seized a moment to declare his willingness to put the state before family, but the emperor still did not trust him.

sentences.zh: 遣阿魯、世傑班日以忠義與之往復論難，益知其心無他，遂聞于帝，帝始無疑。

translations.literal: He dispatched Aru and Shijieban day after day to debate back and forth with him on loyalty and righteousness, and came to know ever more clearly that his heart held no other intent. He then reported this to the emperor, and the emperor at last had no doubts.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Aru and Shijieban to debate loyalty and duty with Toqto'a day after day, and became convinced of his sincerity. He reported this to the emperor, who at last believed him.

sentences.zh: 是年，車駕自上都還京，伯顏數以兵巡行紅城諸處，歸輒在後。

translations.literal: That year, as the imperial carriage returned from Shangdu to the capital, Bayan repeatedly led troops on patrol through the Hongcheng region and always marched behind on the return.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as the emperor returned from Shangdu to the capital, Bayan repeatedly patrolled the Hongcheng region with troops and always brought up the rear on the march home.

sentences.zh: 三人謀益堅，伯顏不知，益逞凶虐，搆陷郯王徹徹篤，奏賜死，帝未允，輒傳旨行刑。

translations.literal: The three men's plot grew ever firmer, but Bayan did not know. He became ever more violent and cruel, framed the Prince of Tan Chechedu, memorialized for his death by imperial grace, and though the emperor had not assented, immediately transmitted an edict and carried out the execution.
translations.idiomatic: The three conspirators grew more resolute, but Bayan knew nothing. He grew ever more brutal, framed the Prince of Tan Chechedu, and memorialized for his death. When the emperor refused, he issued the order himself and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 復奏貶宣讓王帖木兒不花、威順王寬徹普化，辭色憤厲，不待旨而行。

translations.literal: He again memorialized to degrade Prince Xuanrang Temurbuqa and Prince Weishun Kuanchipuhua. His words and expression were fierce and angry, and he acted without awaiting the imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to degrade Prince Xuanrang Temurbuqa and Prince Weishun Kuanchipuhua, speaking with furious insistence and acting without waiting for the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 帝益忿之。

translations.literal: The emperor was increasingly resentful of him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger deepened.

sentences.zh: 伯顏且日益立威，鍛鍊諸獄延及無辜。

translations.literal: Bayan, moreover, daily sought to establish his authority more fiercely, forging cases in the various prisons and extending them to the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan daily sought to intimidate further, fabricating cases that ensnared the innocent.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，伯顏自領兵衛，請帝出田。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year Bayan personally led armed guards and requested that the emperor go out hunting.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year Bayan personally led armed guards and asked the emperor to go hunting.

sentences.zh: 脫脫告帝托疾不往。

translations.literal: Toqto'a advised the emperor to plead illness and not go.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a advised the emperor to plead illness and stay away.

sentences.zh: 伯顏固請太子燕帖古思出次柳林。

translations.literal: Bayan strongly requested that the crown prince Yanchigusi go out and encamp at Liulin.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan insisted that Crown Prince Yanchigusi go out and encamp at Liulin.

sentences.zh: 脫脫欲有所為，遂與世傑班、阿魯合議，白于帝。

translations.literal: Toqto'a wished to take action, and thereupon conferred with Shijieban and Aru and reported to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a planned to act. He conferred with Shijieban and Aru and reported to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，脫脫悉拘門鑰，受密旨領軍，阿魯、世傑班侍帝側傳命。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day Toqto'a seized all the gate keys, received a secret command and led the army, while Aru and Shijieban attended at the emperor's side to transmit orders.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day Toqto'a seized all the gate keys, received secret orders, and took command of the troops, while Aru and Shijieban waited at the emperor's side to relay his commands.

sentences.zh: 是夜，帝御玉德殿，主符檄，發號令，詳見脫脫傳。

translations.literal: That night the emperor presided in the Yude Hall, controlled seals and proclamations, and issued commands; the full account is in the biography of Toqto'a.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor took command in the Yude Hall, issuing seals and orders; the full account appears in Toqto'a's biography.

sentences.zh: 中夜二鼓，遣太子怯薛月可察兒率三十騎抵太子營，取之入城，夜半見帝。

translations.literal: At the second watch of midnight he dispatched the crown prince's kesig Yuekecha'er to lead thirty horsemen to the crown prince's camp, take him, and bring him into the city; at midnight he saw the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch of midnight he sent the crown prince's kesig Yuekecha'er with thirty horsemen to the prince's camp, brought him into the city, and presented him to the emperor at midnight.

sentences.zh: 四鼓，命只兒瓦歹奉詔往柳林，出伯顏為河南行省左丞相。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch he ordered Jirwadai to carry an edict to Liulin and remove Bayan, appointing him Left Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch he ordered Jirwadai to carry an edict to Liulin removing Bayan and appointing him Left Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 己亥，伯顏遣人來城下問故。

translations.literal: On the jihai day Bayan sent men below the city wall to ask the reason.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day Bayan sent men to the city wall to ask what had happened.

sentences.zh: 脫脫倨城門上宣言，有旨黜丞相一人，諸從官無罪，可各還本衛。

translations.literal: Toqto'a stood haughtily atop the gate and proclaimed: "There is an edict dismissing one chief councillor. The various attendant officials are without guilt and may each return to their original guard."
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a stood atop the gate and proclaimed, "By edict one chief councillor is dismissed. His attendants are not guilty and may return to their guards."

sentences.zh: 伯顏奏乞陛辭，不許，遂行。

translations.literal: Bayan memorialized requesting a farewell audience with the throne; this was not permitted, and he thereupon departed.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan asked to bid farewell to the emperor, but permission was refused, and he departed.

sentences.zh: 道出真定，父老奉觴酒以進。

translations.literal: Passing through Zhending, elders offered cups of wine to present to him.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Zhending, local elders offered him wine.

sentences.zh: 伯顏問曰：「爾曾見子殺父事耶？」

translations.literal: Bayan asked: "Have you ever seen a case of a son killing his father?"
translations.idiomatic: Bayan asked, "Have you ever seen a son kill his father?"

sentences.zh: 父老曰：「不曾見子殺父，惟見臣殺君。」

translations.literal: The elders said: "We have never seen a son kill his father; we have only seen a minister kill his ruler."
translations.idiomatic: The elders replied, "We have never seen a son kill his father—only a minister kill his ruler."

sentences.zh: 伯顏俛首有慚色。

translations.literal: Bayan bowed his head with a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan bowed his head, ashamed.

sentences.zh: 三月辛未，詔徙南恩州陽春縣安置，病死于龍興路驛舍。

translations.literal: On the xinwei day of the third month an edict ordered him resettled in Yangchun County, Nan'en Prefecture. He died of illness in a post station on the Longxing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the third month an edict ordered him resettled in Yangchun County, Nan'en Prefecture. He died of illness at a post station in Longxing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 馬札兒台

translations.literal: Mazhaertai
translations.idiomatic: Mazhaertai

sentences.zh: 馬札兒台，世系見兄伯顏傳。

translations.literal: Mazhaertai—his lineage is given in the biography of his elder brother Bayan.
translations.idiomatic: Mazhaertai's lineage is recorded in the biography of his elder brother Bayan.

sentences.zh: 馬札兒台蚤扈從武宗，後侍仁宗於潛邸，出入恭謹，蒞事敏達，仁宗說之。

translations.literal: Mazhaertai early followed and attended Wuzong. Later he served Renzong at the princely residence. In coming and going he was respectful and careful; in handling affairs he was quick and perceptive. Renzong was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Mazhaertai early served Wuzong, then attended Renzong at his princely residence. He was respectful in deportment and quick and capable in affairs, and Renzong was pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 及立為皇太子，以為中順大夫、典用太監。

translations.literal: When he was established as crown prince, Mazhaertai was appointed Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Director of the Directorate of Palace Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was made crown prince, Mazhaertai was appointed Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Director of the Directorate of Palace Supplies.

sentences.zh: 尋遷吏部郎中，陞侍郎，進兵部尚書，遷利用卿，進度支卿，轉同知典瑞院事，陞院使，歷大都路達魯花赤，佩虎符，領虎賁親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to Vice Minister, advanced to Minister of War, transferred to Director of the Directorate of Palace Use, advanced to Director of the Directorate of Revenue, transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Imperial Insignia, promoted to Commissioner, served as darughachi of Dadu Circuit, wore the tiger tally, and directed the Huben Elite Army Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then Vice Minister, then Minister of War, then Director of the Directorate of Palace Use, then Director of the Directorate of Revenue, then Vice Director and Commissioner of the Directorate of Imperial Insignia, served as darughachi of Dadu Circuit with the tiger tally, and commanded the Huben Guard.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年，拜陝西行臺治書侍御史，關陝大饑，賑貸有不及者，盡出私財以周貧民，所活甚衆。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding he was appointed Secretariat Inspector of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat. In Guan and Shaanxi a great famine struck; where relief and loans did not reach, he spent his entire private wealth to succor the poor, and the lives he saved were very many.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taiding he was appointed Secretariat Inspector on the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat. When a severe famine struck Guan and Shaanxi and official relief could not reach everyone, he spent his own fortune to help the destitute and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 轉太府卿，又轉都功德使，改宣政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Storehouse, then transferred to Commissioner of Merit Works, and then made Commissioner of the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Palace Storehouse, then Commissioner of Merit Works, and then Commissioner of the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三遷皆仍太府卿，佩元降虎符，領高麗女直漢軍萬戶府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Through all three transfers he still remained Director of the Palace Storehouse, wore the tiger tally bestowed by the dynasty, and served as darughachi of the Ten-thousand Households Office of the Goryeo, Jurchen, and Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: Through all three promotions he retained the post of Director of the Palace Storehouse, wore the imperial tiger tally, and served as darughachi of the Goryeo, Jurchen, and Han Army Ten-thousand Households Office.

sentences.zh: 拜御史大夫，仍領高麗女直漢軍，兼右衛阿速親軍都指揮使司達魯花赤，提調承徽寺。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Censor, still directing the Goryeo, Jurchen, and Han Army, and concurrently serving as darughachi of the Asud Guard Command of the Right Wing, with supervisory authority over Chenghui Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Censor while continuing to command the Goryeo, Jurchen, and Han Army, and concurrently served as darughachi of the Right Wing Asud Guard Command with supervisory authority over Chenghui Temple.

sentences.zh: 尋遷知樞密院事，兼前職，加提調武備寺事，加金牌，領欽察闖闖帖木兒千戶所；

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Administrator of Military Affairs, retaining his previous posts, with added supervisory authority over Wubei Temple, granted the gold tally, and given charge of the Qipchaq Chanchan Temür Thousand-household Office;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Administrator of Military Affairs while keeping his previous posts, given added supervisory authority over Wubei Temple, granted the gold tally, and put in charge of the Qipchaq Chanchan Temür thousand-household office;

sentences.zh: 又仍以知樞密院事，加鎮守海口侍衛親軍屯儲都指揮使司達魯花赤，餘如故。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Administrator of Military Affairs and additionally made darughachi of the Haikou Guard Army Depot Command, all other posts remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Administrator of Military Affairs and additionally appointed darughachi of the Haikou Guard Army Depot Command, with all other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 馬扎兒台所至不以察察為明，赫赫為威，僚屬各效其勤，至於事功既成，未嘗以為己出也。

translations.literal: Wherever Mazhaertai went, he did not take sharp scrutiny as clarity or imposing display as authority. His subordinates each gave their utmost, and when affairs were successfully accomplished he never claimed the credit for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Mazhaertai served, he did not equate sharp-eyed scrutiny with wisdom or imposing display with authority. His subordinates gave their best, and when work was done well he never took the credit.

sentences.zh: 以仁宗寵遇之深，忌日必先百官詣原廟致敬，或一食一果之美，必持獻廟中。

translations.literal: Because of the deep favor Emperor Renzong had shown him, on the anniversary of Renzong's death he always went before all officials to the ancestral temple to pay homage; even a single delicacy or fruit, he would always carry and offer at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor Renzong had favored him so deeply, on Renzong's death anniversary he always arrived at the ancestral temple ahead of the other officials to pay homage. Even a single choice dish or fruit he would bring and offer at the temple.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘗建寺雲州九峰山，未成而崩，馬扎兒台以私財成之，曰：「是雖未足以報先帝之恩，而先帝嘗駐蹕於茲，誠不忍過其所而坐視蕪廢也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong had once begun building a temple at Jiufeng Mountain in Yunzhou; before it was finished he passed away. Mazhaertai completed it with private wealth, saying: "This is not enough to repay the former emperor's kindness, but the former emperor once halted his carriage here — I truly cannot pass the place where he once tarried and sit watching it fall to ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong had begun building a temple on Jiufeng Mountain in Yunzhou, but died before it was finished. Mazhaertai completed it at his own expense, saying, "This hardly repays the late emperor's kindness, but he once halted here — I cannot pass the spot where he once rested and watch it fall into ruin."

sentences.zh: 又建寺都城健德門東。

translations.literal: He also built a temple east of Jiande Gate in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He also built a temple east of Jiande Gate in the capital.

sentences.zh: 十二年，特命改封德王，令翰林儒臣製詞立碑，仍賜旌忠昭德之額。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was specially ordered enfeoffed as Prince of De. The Hanlin scholar-officials were commanded to compose the inscription for the stele, and he was additionally granted the plaque "Loyalty and Virtue Proclaimed."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was specially enfeoffed as Prince of De. Hanlin scholars were ordered to compose the stele inscription, and he was also granted a plaque reading "Loyalty and Virtue Proclaimed."

sentences.zh: 長子脫脫，次子也先帖木兒。

translations.literal: His eldest son was Toqto'a; his second son Yexiantemur.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Toqto'a; his second son was Yexiantemur.

sentences.zh: 是時，其伯父伯顏為中書右丞相，既誅唐其勢，益無所忌，擅爵人，赦死罪，任邪佞，殺無辜，諸衛精兵收為己用，府庫錢帛聽其出納。

translations.literal: At that time his uncle Bayan was Right Grand Councillor of the Secretariat. After he had executed Tangqishi, he grew ever more fearless. He conferred ranks at will, pardoned capital crimes, employed wicked flatterers, killed the innocent, took the elite troops of the guards for his own use, and had the treasury's money and silk released and received at his word.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his uncle Bayan was Right Grand Councillor. After executing Tangqishi he grew ever bolder: he ennobled men at will, pardoned capital offenders, employed corrupt flatterers, killed the innocent, took the elite guard troops for himself, and treated the treasury as his own.

sentences.zh: 帝積不能平。

translations.literal: The emperor's resentment accumulated beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's resentment built until he could bear it no longer.

sentences.zh: 脫脫雖幼養於伯顏，常憂其敗，私請於其父曰：「伯父驕縱已甚，萬一天子震怒，則吾族赤矣。

translations.literal: Though Toqto'a had been raised from childhood in Bayan's household, he constantly feared his downfall, and privately urged his father: "Uncle's arrogance and license have already gone too far — if the Son of Heaven should be provoked to wrath, our whole clan will be wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Though Toqto'a had been raised in Bayan's household from childhood, he constantly feared disaster and privately urged his father, "Uncle has grown wildly arrogant. If the emperor should be provoked to wrath, our whole clan will be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 曷若於未敗圖之。」

translations.literal: Would it not be better to act before disaster strikes?"
translations.idiomatic: Would it not be better to act before disaster strikes?"

sentences.zh: 其父以為然，復懷疑久未決。

translations.literal: His father agreed, but still harbored doubts and for a long time could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: His father agreed, but still hesitated and for a long time could not decide.

sentences.zh: 質之直方，直方曰：「傳有之，『大義滅親』。

translations.literal: He asked Wu Zhifang's counsel. Zhifang said: "The tradition has it: 'Destroy kin for the sake of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Wu Zhifang's advice. Zhifang said, "The tradition tells us: 'Righteousness may require destroying one's own kin.

sentences.zh: 大夫但知忠於國家耳，餘復何顧焉。」

translations.literal: You, sir, need only know loyalty to the state — what else is there to consider?"
translations.idiomatic: You need only be loyal to the state — what else is there to weigh?"

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝之左右前後皆伯顏所樹親黨，獨世傑班、阿魯為帝腹心，日與之處。

translations.literal: At that time those around the emperor on all sides were all partisans Bayan had planted. Only Shijieban and Aru were the emperor's trusted intimates, with whom he daily associated.
translations.idiomatic: At that time everyone around the emperor was a partisan Bayan had placed there. Only Shijieban and Aru were the emperor's trusted intimates, and he saw them daily.

sentences.zh: 脫脫遂與二人深相結納。

translations.literal: Toqto'a thereupon formed a deep bond with the two men.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a then formed a close alliance with the two men.

sentences.zh: 而錢唐楊瑀嘗事帝潛邸，為奎章閣廣成局副使，得出入禁中，帝知其可用，每三人論事，使瑀參焉。

translations.literal: Yang Yu of Qiantang had once served the emperor at his princely residence; he was Deputy Commissioner of the Kuizhang Pavilion Guangcheng Bureau and could enter and leave the forbidden inner quarters. The emperor knew he could be relied upon; whenever the three men discussed affairs, he had Yu take part.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu of Qiantang had served the emperor at his princely residence and was Deputy Commissioner of the Kuizhang Pavilion Guangcheng Bureau, with access to the inner palace. Knowing him trustworthy, the emperor had Yu join whenever the three men met to discuss affairs.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，車駕留上都，伯顏時出赴應昌。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year the imperial carriage remained at Shangdu while Bayan went out to Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year the emperor remained at Shangdu while Bayan went out to Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 脫脫與世傑班、阿魯謀欲禦之東門外，懼弗勝而止。

translations.literal: Toqto'a, Shijieban, and Aru planned to intercept him outside the eastern gate, but fearing they would not prevail, they desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a, Shijieban, and Aru planned to intercept him outside the eastern gate, but fearing they would not prevail, they abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 會河南范孟矯殺省臣，事連廉訪使段輔，伯顏風臺臣言漢人不可為廉訪使。

translations.literal: It happened that Fan Meng of Henan forged orders and killed the provincial officials; the affair implicated the surveillance commissioner Duan Fu. Bayan prompted the censorial officials to declare that Han Chinese could not serve as surveillance commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Then Fan Meng of Henan forged orders and murdered the provincial officials, implicating surveillance commissioner Duan Fu. Bayan prompted the censorial officials to argue that Han Chinese should not serve as surveillance commissioners.

sentences.zh: 時別兒怯不花亦為御史大夫，畏人之議己，辭疾不出，故其章未上。

translations.literal: At that time Bie'erqiebuhua was also Grand Censor. Fearing others would criticize him, he pleaded illness and did not appear, so the memorial was not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Bie'erqiebuhua was also Grand Censor. Fearing criticism, he pleaded illness and stayed away, so the memorial had not yet been submitted.

sentences.zh: 伯顏促之急，監察御史以告脫脫。

translations.literal: Bayan pressed urgently. A supervising censor reported this to Toqto'a.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan pressed the matter urgently. A supervising censor reported this to Toqto'a.

sentences.zh: 脫脫曰：「別兒怯不花位吾上，且掌印，我安敢專邪？」

translations.literal: Toqto'a said: "Bie'erqiebuhua ranks above me and moreover holds the seal — how dare I act alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a said, "Bie'erqiebuhua outranks me and holds the seal — how dare I act on my own?"

sentences.zh: 別兒怯不花聞之懼，且將出。

translations.literal: When Bie'erqiebuhua heard of this he was afraid and was about to go out.
translations.idiomatic: When Bie'erqiebuhua heard this he was frightened and prepared to go forward.

sentences.zh: 脫脫度不能遏，謀於直方。

translations.literal: Toqto'a saw he could not stop it and consulted Wu Zhifang.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a saw he could not stop it and consulted Wu Zhifang.

sentences.zh: 直方曰：「此祖宗法度，決不可廢，盍先為上言之。」

translations.literal: Zhifang said: "This is ancestral law and institution — it absolutely cannot be abolished. Why not first speak of it to the emperor?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang said, "This is ancestral law and must not be abolished. Why not speak to the emperor first?"

sentences.zh: 脫脫入告于帝，及章上，帝如脫脫言。

translations.literal: Toqto'a entered and reported to the emperor; when the memorial was submitted, the emperor took Toqto'a's view.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a went in and reported to the emperor; when the memorial was submitted, the emperor sided with Toqto'a.

sentences.zh: 伯顏知出於脫脫，大怒，言於帝曰：「脫脫雖臣之子，其心專佑漢人，必當治之。」

translations.literal: Bayan knew this came from Toqto'a and was greatly angered. He said to the emperor: "Though Toqto'a is my nephew, his heart is wholly set on shielding the Han — he must be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Bayan knew Toqto'a was behind it and was furious. He told the emperor, "Though Toqto'a is my nephew, his heart is wholly with the Han — he must be punished."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此皆朕意，非脫脫罪也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is entirely my will; it is not Toqto'a's crime."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is entirely my decision — Toqto'a is not at fault."

sentences.zh: 及伯顏擅貶宣讓、威順二王，帝不勝其忿，決意逐之。

translations.literal: When Bayan on his own authority demoted the Princes of Xuanrang and Weishun, the emperor could not contain his rage and resolved to expel him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan on his own authority demoted the Princes of Xuanrang and Weishun, the emperor's fury overflowed and he resolved to drive Bayan out.

sentences.zh: 一日，泣語脫脫，脫脫亦泣下，歸與直方謀。

translations.literal: One day he wept as he spoke with Toqto'a; Toqto'a wept as well and returned home to plan with Zhifang.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor wept as he spoke with Toqto'a. Toqto'a wept too, then went home to plan with Zhifang.

sentences.zh: 直方曰：「此宗社安危所繫，不可不密。

translations.literal: Zhifang said: "This concerns the safety of state and altars — secrecy is indispensable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang said, "This concerns the fate of the dynasty — secrecy is essential.

sentences.zh: 議論之際，左右為誰？」

translations.literal: At the time of deliberation, who will be at your side?"
translations.idiomatic: When you discuss this, who will be at your side?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「阿魯及脫脫木兒。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Aru and Tuotuomur."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Aru and Tuotuomur."

sentences.zh: 直方曰：「子之伯父，挾震主之威，此輩苟利富貴，其語一泄，則主危身戮矣。」

translations.literal: Zhifang said: "Your uncle wields the awe of one who controls the ruler — if these men, for the sake of wealth and rank, should let a word slip, the sovereign will be endangered and you will be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang said, "Your uncle holds the awe of a man who controls his ruler. If these men, tempted by wealth and rank, let a word slip, the emperor will be endangered and you will be killed."

sentences.zh: 脫脫乃延二人于家，置酒張樂，晝夜不令出。

translations.literal: Toqto'a then invited the two men to his house, set out wine and music, and would not let them leave day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a then invited the two men to his house, entertained them with wine and music, and kept them there day and night.

sentences.zh: 遂與世傑班、阿魯議，候伯顏入朝禽之。

translations.literal: He then deliberated with Shijieban and Aru to wait until Bayan entered court and seize him.
translations.idiomatic: He then plotted with Shijieban and Aru to seize Bayan when he came to court.

sentences.zh: 戒衛士嚴宮門出入，螭坳悉為置兵。

translations.literal: He warned the guards to tighten control over entry and exit at the palace gates, and placed soldiers throughout the outer court at the imperial steps.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the guards to tighten control over the palace gates and posted soldiers throughout the outer court at the imperial steps.

sentences.zh: 伯顏見之大驚，召脫脫責之。

translations.literal: When Bayan saw this he was greatly alarmed and summoned Toqto'a to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan was greatly alarmed and summoned Toqto'a to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「天子所居，防禦不得不爾。」

translations.literal: Toqto'a replied: "At the place where the Son of Heaven dwells, defenses cannot be other than this."
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a replied, "Where the Son of Heaven dwells, defenses cannot be less than this."

sentences.zh: 伯顏遂疑脫脫，益增兵自衛。

translations.literal: Bayan then suspected Toqto'a and increased his guard for self-protection.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan then grew suspicious of Toqto'a and increased his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，伯顏請太子燕帖古思獵于柳林。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year Bayan requested that Crown Prince Yanchigusi go hunting at Liulin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year Bayan asked that Crown Prince Yanchigusi go hunting at Liulin.

sentences.zh: 脫脫與世傑班、阿魯合謀以所掌兵及宿衛士拒伯顏。

translations.literal: Toqto'a together with Shijieban and Aru plotted to use the troops under their command and the palace guards to resist Bayan.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a, Shijieban, and Aru plotted to use the troops under their command and the palace guards to resist Bayan.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，遂拘京城門鑰，命所親信列布城門下。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day they seized the keys to the capital gates and stationed trusted men at each gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day they seized the keys to the capital gates and posted trusted men at every gate.

sentences.zh: 是夜，奉帝御玉德殿，召近臣汪家奴，沙剌班及省院大臣先後入見，出五門聽命。

translations.literal: That night they conducted the emperor to the Yude Hall, summoning the close attendant Wangjianu, Shaban, and the grand councillors of the secretariat and the administrators of military affairs in succession to audience; they were sent out the Five Gates to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: That night they escorted the emperor to the Yude Hall and summoned the close attendants Wangjianu and Shaban and the secretariat and military-affairs ministers in turn for audience, then sent them out the Five Gates to await orders.

sentences.zh: 又召瑀及江西范匯入草詔，數伯顏罪狀。

translations.literal: Yang Yu and Fan Hui of Jiangxi were also summoned to draft the edict enumerating Bayan's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu and Fan Hui of Jiangxi were also summoned to draft the edict listing Bayan's crimes.

sentences.zh: 詔成，夜已四鼓，命中書平章政事只兒瓦歹齎赴柳林。

translations.literal: When the edict was complete, the night had already reached the fourth watch; the emperor ordered Central Secretariat Grand Councillor Jierwadai to carry it to Liulin.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was finished it was already the fourth watch of the night. The emperor ordered Central Secretariat Grand Councillor Jierwadai to carry it to Liulin.

sentences.zh: 己亥，脫脫坐城門上，而伯顏亦遣騎士至城下問故。

translations.literal: On the jihai day Toqto'a sat atop the city gate, and Bayan also sent horsemen to the foot of the wall to ask the reason.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day Toqto'a sat atop the city gate while Bayan sent horsemen to the foot of the wall to ask what was happening.

sentences.zh: 脫脫曰：「有旨逐丞相。」

translations.literal: Toqto'a said: "There is an edict dismissing the chief councillor."
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a said, "There is an edict dismissing the chief councillor."

sentences.zh: 伯顏所領諸衛兵皆散，而伯顏遂南行。

translations.literal: The guard troops Bayan commanded all dispersed, and Bayan then went south.
translations.idiomatic: The guard troops under Bayan's command all dispersed, and Bayan departed south.

sentences.zh: 詳見伯顏傳中。

translations.literal: The detailed account appears in Bayan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Bayan's biography.

sentences.zh: 事定，詔以馬扎兒台為中書右丞相；

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, an edict appointed Mazhaertai Right Grand Councillor of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, an edict appointed Mazhaertai Right Grand Councillor;

sentences.zh: 脫脫知樞密院事，虎符，忠翊衛親軍都指揮使，提調武備寺、阿速衛千戶所，兼紹熙等處軍民宣撫都緫使、宣忠兀羅思護衛親軍都指揮使司達魯花赤、昭功萬戶府都緫使。

translations.literal: Toqto'a was made Administrator of Military Affairs with the tiger tally, commander of the Zhongyi Guard, with supervisory authority over Wubei Temple and the Asud Guard thousand-household office, and concurrently Commissioner for Civil and Military Pacification of Shaoxi and other places, darughachi of the Xuanzhong Ulus Guard Command, and Commissioner of the Zhaogong Ten-thousand Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a was made Administrator of Military Affairs with the tiger tally, commander of the Zhongyi Guard, with supervisory authority over Wubei Temple and the Asud Guard thousand-household office, and concurrently Civil and Military Pacification Commissioner for Shaoxi and other districts, darughachi of the Xuanzhong Ulus Guard Command, and Commissioner of the Zhaogong Ten-thousand Households Office.

sentences.zh: 十月，馬扎兒台移疾辭相位，詔以太師就第。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Mazhaertai, pleading illness, resigned the chief councillorship; an edict ordered him to assume the post of Grand Preceptor at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Mazhaertai resigned the chief councillorship on grounds of illness; an edict made him Grand Preceptor and ordered him to remain at his residence.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔修遼、金、宋三史，命脫脫為都緫裁官。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict ordered the compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song, and Toqto'a was appointed chief supervisory editor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict ordered the compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song, and Toqto'a was appointed chief editor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 又請修至正條格頒天下。

translations.literal: He also requested that the Zhizheng Code be revised and promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that the Zhizheng legal code be revised and promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗御宣文閣，脫脫前奏曰：「陛下臨御以來，天下無事，宜留心聖學。

translations.literal: The emperor once held audience at the Xuanwen Pavilion. Toqto'a advanced and memorialized: "Since Your Majesty began your rule, the realm has been at peace — you should attend to sacred learning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once held audience at the Xuanwen Pavilion. Toqto'a stepped forward and said, "Since Your Majesty began your reign the realm has been at peace — you should devote yourself to the study of the sages.

sentences.zh: 頗聞左右多沮撓者，設使經史不足觀，世祖豈以是教裕皇哉？」

translations.literal: I hear that many of those around you obstruct this. Even if the classics and histories were unworthy of study, would the Founding Emperor have used them to instruct Crown Prince Yuzong?"
translations.idiomatic: I hear that many around you discourage it. Even if the classics and histories were unworthy of study, would Kublai have used them to instruct Crown Prince Yuzong?"

sentences.zh: 即祕書監取裕宗所授書以進，帝大悅。

translations.literal: He immediately had the Directorate of Palace Archives fetch the books the Heir Apparent Yuzong had been taught and present them; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately had the Directorate of Palace Archives fetch the books Crown Prince Yuzong had studied and present them to the emperor, who was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 皇太子愛猷識理達臘嘗保育于脫脫家，每有疾飲藥，必嘗之而進。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Ayurshiridara had once been fostered in Toqto'a's household; whenever he fell ill and took medicine, Toqto'a would always taste it before presenting it.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Ayurshiridara had been raised in Toqto'a's household. Whenever the prince fell ill and took medicine, Toqto'a always tasted it first before giving it to him.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗駐蹕雲州，遇烈風暴雨，山水大至，車馬人畜皆漂溺，脫脫抱皇太子單騎登山，乃免。

translations.literal: The emperor once halted at Yunzhou; fierce wind and violent rain struck, and floodwaters from the mountains rose high — horses, carts, men, and livestock were all swept away and drowned. Toqto'a, carrying the crown prince, rode alone up the mountain and thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once halted at Yunzhou when a violent storm struck and mountain floods swept away horses, carts, men, and livestock. Toqto'a, carrying the crown prince, rode alone up the mountain and escaped.

sentences.zh: 至六歲還，帝慰撫之曰：「汝之勤勞，朕不忘也。」

translations.literal: When the prince returned at age six, the emperor comforted Toqto'a and said: "Your toil — I shall not forget it."
translations.idiomatic: When the prince returned home at age six, the emperor comforted Toqto'a and said, "Your devotion — I shall not forget it."

sentences.zh: 脫脫乃以私財造大壽元忠國寺於健德門外，為皇太子祝釐，其費為鈔十二萬二千錠。

translations.literal: Toqto'a thereupon built the Dashou Yuanzhong Guo Temple outside Jiande Gate with private wealth to pray for the crown prince's blessing; the cost was one hundred twenty-two thousand ding of paper notes.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a then built the Dashou Yuanzhong Guo Temple outside Jiande Gate at his own expense to pray for the crown prince's blessing, at a cost of one hundred twenty-two thousand ding of paper notes.

sentences.zh: 四年閏月，領宣政院事。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month of the fourth year he assumed charge of the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month of the fourth year he took charge of the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 諸山主僧請復僧司，且曰：「郡縣所苦，如坐地獄。」

translations.literal: Chief monks from the various mountains petitioned to restore the monastic registry office, saying: "What the commanderies and counties suffer is like sitting in hell."
translations.idiomatic: Chief monks from the various mountains petitioned to restore the monastic registry office, saying, "What the commanderies and counties suffer is like sitting in hell."

sentences.zh: 脫脫曰：「若復僧司，何異地獄中復置地獄邪？」

translations.literal: Toqto'a said: "If the monastic registry is restored, how is that different from setting up another hell within hell?"
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a said, "If the monastic registry is restored, how is that different from building another hell inside hell?"

sentences.zh: 時有疾漸羸，且術者亦言年月不利，乃上表辭位，帝不允，表凡十七上始從之。

translations.literal: At that time his illness was gradually wasting him, and diviners also said the year and month were unfavorable; he submitted a memorial resigning his post. The emperor did not approve; only after seventeen memorials did he finally consent.
translations.idiomatic: By then his illness was gradually wasting him away, and diviners also said the year and month were unfavorable. He submitted a memorial resigning his post, but the emperor refused. Only after seventeen memorials did he finally consent.

sentences.zh: 有旨封鄭王，食邑安豐，賞賚巨萬，俱辭不受。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng with a fief at Anfeng, and rewarded him with vast gifts — all of which he declined.
translations.idiomatic: An edict offered to enfeoff him as Prince of Zheng with a fief at Anfeng and reward him with vast gifts, but he declined them all.

sentences.zh: 乃賜松江田，為立稻田提領所以領之。

translations.literal: He was then granted fields in Songjiang, and a rice-field supervisory office was established to administer them.
translations.idiomatic: He was then granted fields in Songjiang, and a rice-field supervisory office was established to manage them.

sentences.zh: 七年，別兒怯不花為右丞相，以宿憾譖其父馬扎兒台。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Bie'erqiebuhua became Right Grand Councillor and, on account of an old grudge, slandered Toqto'a's father Mazhaertai.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Bie'erqiebuhua became Right Grand Councillor and, nursing an old grudge, slandered Toqto'a's father Mazhaertai.

sentences.zh: 詔徙甘肅。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him resettled to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him exiled to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 脫脫力請俱行，在道則閱騎乘廬帳，食則視其品之精粗，及至其地，馬扎兒台安之。

translations.literal: Toqto'a strongly pleaded to accompany him on the journey. On the road he inspected mounts and tents; at meals he examined the quality of the fare; and when they reached their destination Mazhaertai was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a strongly pleaded to go with him. On the road he inspected the horses and tents; at meals he checked the quality of the food; and when they reached their destination Mazhaertai was content.

sentences.zh: 復移西域撒思之地，至河，召還甘州就養。

translations.literal: He was then moved to Sasin in the Western Regions; when they reached the river, he was recalled to Ganzhou to receive support.
translations.idiomatic: He was then moved to Sasin in the Western Regions, but when they reached the river he was recalled to Ganzhou to be cared for.

sentences.zh: 十一月，馬扎兒台薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Mazhaertai died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Mazhaertai died.

sentences.zh: 帝念脫脫勳勞，召還京師。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of Toqto'a's achievements, summoned him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Toqto'a's service, the emperor summoned him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 八年，命脫脫為太傅，提調宮傅，綜理東宮之事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Toqto'a was appointed Grand Preceptor and given supervisory authority over the palace tutors, comprehensively managing affairs of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Toqto'a was appointed Grand Preceptor, given supervisory authority over the palace tutors, and put in charge of Eastern Palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，朶兒只、太平皆罷相，遂詔脫脫復為中書右丞相，賜上尊、名馬、襲衣、玉帶。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Duo'erzhi and Taiping were both dismissed as chief councillors; an edict then ordered Toqto'a restored as Right Grand Councillor of the Secretariat, granting him fine wine, famous horses, ceremonial robes, and a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Duo'erzhi and Taiping were both dismissed as chief councillors. An edict then restored Toqto'a as Right Grand Councillor and granted him fine wine, famous horses, ceremonial robes, and a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 脫脫既復入中書，恩怨無不報。

translations.literal: Once Toqto'a had reentered the Secretariat, no debt of kindness or enmity went unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Once Toqto'a was back in the Secretariat, he settled every score — of gratitude and of grievance alike.

sentences.zh: 時開端本堂，皇太子學於其中，命脫脫領端本堂事。

translations.literal: At that time the Hall of the Correct Root was opened; the crown prince studied there, and Toqto'a was ordered to direct Hall of the Correct Root affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Hall of the Correct Root was opened for the crown prince's studies, and Toqto'a was ordered to head it.

sentences.zh: 又提調阿速、欽察二衛、內史府、宣政院、太醫院事。

translations.literal: He was also given supervisory authority over the Asud and Qipchaq guards, the Inner Secretariat, the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs, and the Imperial Medical Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given supervisory authority over the Asud and Qipchaq guards, the Inner Secretariat, the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs, and the Imperial Medical Service.

sentences.zh: 十年五月，居母薊國夫人憂。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the tenth year he was in mourning for his mother, Lady Ji of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the tenth year he went into mourning for his mother, Lady Ji of the State.

sentences.zh: 帝遣近臣喻之，俾出理庶務。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a close attendant to instruct him and ordered him to leave mourning and attend to public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a close attendant to tell him to leave mourning and resume public duties.

sentences.zh: 於是脫脫用烏古孫良楨、龔伯遂、汝中柏、伯帖木兒等為僚屬，皆委以腹心之寄，小大之事悉與之謀，事行而群臣不知也。

translations.literal: Toqto'a thereupon employed Wugusun Liangzhen, Gong Bosui, Ru Zhongbai, Bo Temur, and others as subordinates, entrusting them all with his innermost confidence; affairs great and small he deliberated on with them entirely, and when actions were taken the other ministers did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a then took Wugusun Liangzhen, Gong Bosui, Ru Zhongbai, Bo Temur, and others as his staff, entrusting them with his full confidence. He consulted them on everything, great and small, and when decisions were carried out the rest of the court often knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書偰哲篤建言更造至正交鈔，脫脫信之，詔集樞密院、御史臺、翰林、集賢院諸臣議之，皆唯唯而已，獨祭酒呂思誠言其不可，脫脫不悅。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Xi Zhedu proposed reissuing the Zhizheng paper notes. Toqto'a believed him. An edict summoned the officials of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Censorate, the Hanlin Academy, and the Academy of Gathered Worthies to discuss it; all merely assented, but only Academician Lü Sicheng said it could not be done. Toqto'a was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Xi Zhedu proposed reissuing the Zhizheng paper currency. Toqto'a believed him and ordered officials from the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Censorate, the Hanlin Academy, and the Academy of Gathered Worthies to discuss the plan. All merely assented, but Academician Lü Sicheng alone objected. Toqto'a was displeased.

sentences.zh: 既而終變鈔法，而鈔竟不行。

translations.literal: In the end the currency system was changed, but the new notes ultimately could not be put into circulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the currency system was changed, but the new notes never took hold.

sentences.zh: 事見思誠傳。

translations.literal: The account appears in Sicheng's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Lü Sicheng's biography.

sentences.zh: 河決白茅堤，又決金堤，方數千里，民被其患，五年不能塞。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst the Baimao Dike and then burst the Jindi Dike; over several thousand square li the people suffered the disaster, and for five years it could not be sealed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River burst the Baimao Dike and then the Jindi Dike. Over thousands of square li the people suffered, and for five years the breaches could not be sealed.

sentences.zh: 脫脫用賈魯計請塞之，以身任其事。

translations.literal: Toqto'a adopted Jia Lu's plan and requested that the breaches be sealed, taking personal responsibility for the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a adopted Jia Lu's plan to seal the breaches and took personal charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 出告群臣曰：「皇帝方憂下民，為大臣者職當分憂。

translations.literal: He went out and told the ministers: "The emperor is now concerned for the common people — as grand ministers our duty is to share his burden.
translations.idiomatic: He told the ministers, "The emperor is troubled for the people — as his chief ministers it is our duty to share that burden.

sentences.zh: 然事有難為，猶疾有難治，自古河患即難治之疾也，今我必欲去其疾。」

translations.literal: Yet some affairs are hard to accomplish, just as some illnesses are hard to cure — since ancient times river disasters have been illnesses hard to cure, and now I am determined to remove this illness."
translations.idiomatic: Yet some tasks are hard to accomplish, as some illnesses are hard to cure. Since ancient times river disasters have been just such an illness, and I am determined to cure it."

sentences.zh: 而人人異論，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Everyone had a different opinion, but he listened to none of them.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone had a different opinion, but he would hear none of them.

sentences.zh: 乃奏以賈魯為工部尚書，緫治河防，使發河南北兵民十七萬役之，築決堤成，使復故道。

translations.literal: He then memorialized appointing Jia Lu Minister of Works with overall charge of river defenses, ordering one hundred seventy thousand soldiers and civilians north and south of the Yellow River to labor on the project; the breached dikes were built up and the river was restored to its old course.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized appointing Jia Lu Minister of Works with overall charge of river defenses, mobilizing one hundred seventy thousand soldiers and civilians north and south of the Yellow River. The breached dikes were rebuilt and the river restored to its old course.

sentences.zh: 凡八月功成。

translations.literal: In all, the work was completed in eight months.
translations.idiomatic: The work was completed in eight months.

sentences.zh: 事見河渠志。

translations.literal: The account appears in the Treatise on Rivers and Canals.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the Treatise on Rivers and Canals.

sentences.zh: 於是天子嘉其功，賜世襲荅剌罕之號。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven praised his achievement and granted him the title of Darqan as a hereditary honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then praised his achievement and granted him the hereditary title of Darqan.

sentences.zh: 又敕儒臣歐陽玄製河平碑以載其功。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Confucian minister Ouyang Xuan to compose a stele on the pacification of the river to record his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the scholar-official Ouyang Xuan to compose a stele commemorating the river's pacification.

sentences.zh: 仍賜淮安路為其食邑，郡邑長吏聽其自用。

translations.literal: He further granted Huai'an Circuit as his fief for sustenance, and the prefectural and district magistrates were permitted to be appointed at his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: He further granted Huai'an Circuit as his personal fief, and local magistrates were to be appointed at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 已而汝、潁之間妖寇聚衆反，以紅巾為號，襄、樊、唐、鄧皆起而應之。

translations.literal: Before long, demonic bandits between Ru and Ying gathered masses and rebelled, taking the Red Turbans as their name; Xiang, Fan, Tang, and Deng all rose in response.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, rebel bandits between the Ru and Ying rivers rose in force under the banner of the Red Turbans, and uprisings spread through Xiangyang, Fan, Tang, and Deng.

sentences.zh: 十一年，脫脫乃奏以弟御史大夫也先帖木兒為知樞密院事，將諸衛兵十餘萬討之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Toqto'a memorialized appointing his younger brother, Censor-in-Chief Yexiantemur, as Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, leading more than one hundred thousand guardsmen to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Toqto'a memorialized appointing his younger brother Yexiantemur, Censor-in-Chief, as Administrator of Military Affairs and dispatching more than one hundred thousand guardsmen against them.

sentences.zh: 克上蔡。

translations.literal: He captured Shangcai.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Shangcai.

sentences.zh: 既而駐兵沙河，軍中夜驚。

translations.literal: Subsequently he encamped at Shahe, and the army was startled at night.
translations.idiomatic: He then encamped at Shahe, where the army panicked one night.

sentences.zh: 也先帖木兒盡棄軍資器械，北奔汴梁，收散卒，屯朱仙鎮。

translations.literal: Yexiantemur abandoned all military stores and equipment, fled north to Bianliang, gathered scattered troops, and encamped at Zhuxian Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yexiantemur abandoned all army supplies and equipment, fled north to Bianliang, regrouped scattered troops, and encamped at Zhuxian Zhen.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以也先帖木兒不習兵，詔別將代之。

translations.literal: The court, considering Yexiantemur unskilled in warfare, decreed that another general replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Deeming Yexiantemur unfit for command, the court ordered another general to take his place.

sentences.zh: 也先帖木兒徑歸，昏夜入城，仍為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Yexiantemur returned directly, entered the city at dark, and remained Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yexiantemur returned directly, entered the city under cover of night, and retained his post as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 陝西行臺監察御史十二人劾其喪師辱國之罪，脫脫怒，乃遷西行臺御史大夫朶兒直班為湖廣行省平章政事，而御史皆除各府添設判官，由是人皆莫敢言事。

translations.literal: Twelve supervising censors of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat impeached him for the crime of losing the army and shaming the state. Toqto'a was angered and transferred Branch Secretariat Censor-in-Chief Duo'erzhiban to be Pacification Commissioner of Huguang Branch Secretariat, while all the censors were dismissed to serve as additionally appointed assistant magistrates in various prefectures — whereupon none dared speak up on matters.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve supervising censors of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat impeached him for losing the army and disgracing the state. Toqto'a was furious. He transferred Branch Secretariat Censor-in-Chief Duo'erzhiban to Pacification Commissioner of Huguang and demoted all the censors to additional assistant magistrate posts in various prefectures. From then on no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 十二年，紅巾有號芝麻李者，據徐州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, among the Red Turbans there was one called Sesame Li who seized Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year a Red Turban leader known as Sesame Li seized Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 脫脫請自行討之，以逯魯曾為淮南宣慰使，募鹽丁及城邑趫捷，通二萬人，與所統兵俱發。

translations.literal: Toqto'a requested to lead the campaign himself; appointing Luluan Pacification Commissioner of Huainan, he recruited salt laborers and agile townsmen, altogether twenty thousand men, and set out together with the troops under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a asked to lead the campaign himself. He appointed Luluan Pacification Commissioner of Huainan, recruited salt laborers and able townsmen — twenty thousand in all — and marched out with his own troops.

sentences.zh: 九月，師次徐州，攻其西門。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the army halted at Xuzhou and attacked its west gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army reached Xuzhou and assaulted the west gate.

sentences.zh: 賊出戰，以鐵翎箭射馬首，脫脫不為動，麾軍奮擊之，大破其衆，入其外郛。

translations.literal: The rebels came out to fight and shot iron-feathered arrows at his horse's head; Toqto'a did not stir, waved his troops on in fierce attack, routed their forces, and entered the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sallied out and shot iron-feathered arrows at his horse's head, but Toqto'a did not flinch. He waved his troops forward, routed the enemy, and pushed into the outer city.

sentences.zh: 明日，大兵四集，亟攻之，賊不能支，城破，芝麻李遁去。

translations.literal: The next day the great armies gathered on all sides and pressed the attack urgently; the rebels could not hold, the city fell, and Sesame Li fled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day reinforcements converged from all sides and pressed the assault. The rebels could not hold; the city fell and Sesame Li fled.

sentences.zh: 獲其黃繖旗鼓，燒其積聚，追擒其偽千戶數十人，遂屠其城。

translations.literal: They seized his yellow parasol, banners, and drums, burned his stored supplies, pursued and captured dozens of his false thousand-household commanders, and then massacred the city.
translations.idiomatic: They seized his yellow imperial parasol, banners, and drums, burned his stored provisions, captured dozens of rebel thousand-household commanders in pursuit, and then put the city to the sword.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中書平章政事普化等即軍中命脫脫為太師，依前右丞相，趣還朝，而以樞密院同知禿赤等進師平潁、亳。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Secretariat Pacification Commissioner Puhua and others to the army to appoint Toqto'a Grand Preceptor, retaining his previous post as Right Grand Councillor, urging him to return to court, while Associate Administrator of Military Affairs Tuqi and others advanced the army to pacify Ying and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Secretariat Pacification Commissioner Puhua and others to the camp to appoint Toqto'a Grand Preceptor while keeping him as Right Grand Councillor, ordering him to hurry back to court while Associate Administrator Tuqi and others pushed on to pacify Ying and Bo.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜上尊、珠衣、白金、寶鞍。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted fine wine, pearl-inlaid robes, white gold, and a precious saddle.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was rewarded with fine wine, pearl-inlaid robes, silver, and a jeweled saddle.

sentences.zh: 皇太子錫燕于私第。

translations.literal: The crown prince bestowed a banquet at his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince hosted a banquet at his private residence in his honor.

sentences.zh: 詔改徐州為武安州，而立碑以著其績。

translations.literal: An edict changed Xuzhou to Wu'an Prefecture and erected a stele to record his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed Xuzhou Wu'an Prefecture and erected a stele commemorating his victory.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月，脫脫用左丞烏古孫良楨、右丞悟良哈台議，屯田京畿，以二人兼大司農卿，而脫脫領大司農事。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year, Toqto'a adopted the proposals of Left Councillor Wugusun Liangzhen and Right Councillor Wulianghatai to establish garrison farms in the capital region; the two were concurrently made Ministers of the Grand Revenues, while Toqto'a headed Grand Revenues affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year Toqto'a, acting on proposals from Left Councillor Wugusun Liangzhen and Right Councillor Wulianghatai, ordered garrison farming in the capital region. Both men were concurrently appointed Ministers of Grand Revenues while Toqto'a himself headed the ministry.

sentences.zh: 西至西山，東至遷民鎮，南至保定、河間，北至檀、順州，皆引水利，立法佃種，歲乃大稔。

translations.literal: From the Western Hills in the west to Qianmin Zhen in the east, from Baoding and Hejian in the south to Tan and Shun prefectures in the north — everywhere waterworks were introduced, laws were established for tenant cultivation, and the year brought a great harvest.
