translations.idiomatic: From the Western Hills in the west to Qianmin Zhen in the east, from Baoding and Hejian in the south to Tan and Shun prefectures in the north — irrigated fields were opened by law, and the year brought a bumper harvest.

sentences.zh: 十四年，張士誠據高郵，屢招諭之不降，詔脫脫緫制諸王諸省軍討之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Zhang Shicheng held Gaoyou; though repeatedly summoned and admonished, he would not submit. An edict ordered Toqto'a to take overall command of the armies of princes and provinces to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Zhang Shicheng held Gaoyou. Despite repeated summons he refused to submit, and an edict put Toqto'a in overall command of the armies of princes and provinces to subdue him.

sentences.zh: 黜陟予奪一切庶政，悉聽便宜行事；

translations.literal: Promotions, dismissals, rewards, and punishments, and all other routine administration, were entirely at his discretion to act as expedient;
translations.idiomatic: Promotions, dismissals, rewards, and punishments — all routine administration — were entirely at his discretion;

sentences.zh: 省臺院部諸司聽選官屬；

translations.literal: the Branch Secretariats, Censorate, Bureau of Military Affairs, ministries, and all other offices were permitted to select their own subordinates;
translations.idiomatic: branch secretariats, the Censorate, military bureaus, ministries, and all other offices could choose their own staff;

sentences.zh: 從行稟受節制。

translations.literal: those accompanying him were to receive orders and submit to his authority.
translations.idiomatic: and everyone on campaign was subject to his command.

sentences.zh: 西域、西番皆發兵來助。

translations.literal: From the Western Regions and Xifan, troops were all dispatched to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were dispatched from the Western Regions and Tibet to assist.

sentences.zh: 旌旗累千里，金鼓震野，出師之盛，未有過之者。

translations.literal: Banners and flags stretched for a thousand li, gold drums shook the fields — none had ever seen a campaign launched on so grand a scale.
translations.idiomatic: Banners stretched for a thousand li and war drums shook the countryside — never had a campaign been launched on so magnificent a scale.

sentences.zh: 師次濟寧，遣官詣闕里祀孔子，過鄒縣祀孟子。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jining; officials were sent to Queli to sacrifice to Confucius, and passing Zou County they sacrificed to Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Jining. Officials were sent to Queli to sacrifice to Confucius, and at Zou County to sacrifice to Mencius.

sentences.zh: 十一月，至高郵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month they reached Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they reached Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 辛未至乙酉，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: From xinwei to yiyou, in successive battles they were victorious.
translations.idiomatic: From xinwei to yiyou they won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 分遣兵平六合，賊勢大蹙。

translations.literal: Troops were dispatched separately to pacify Luhe, and the rebel forces were greatly compressed.
translations.idiomatic: Detachments were sent to pacify Luhe, and the rebels were driven into a corner.

sentences.zh: 俄有詔罪其老師費財，以河南行省左丞相太不花、中書平章政事月闊察兒、知樞密院事雪雪代將其兵，削其官爵，安置淮安。

translations.literal: Suddenly an edict faulted him for keeping the army in the field too long and wasting resources; Henan Branch Secretariat Left Grand Councillor Tarbuka, Secretariat Pacification Commissioner Yuekuochae'r, and Administrator of Military Affairs Xuexue were ordered to replace him in command of his troops, his titles and ranks were stripped, and he was confined at Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly an edict blamed him for keeping the army idle too long at ruinous expense. Henan Left Grand Councillor Tarbuka, Secretariat Pacification Commissioner Yuekuochae'r, and Military Affairs Administrator Xuexue replaced him in command; his titles were stripped and he was confined at Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 先是，脫脫之西行也，別兒怯不花欲陷之死。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Toqto'a was on his western expedition, Bie'erqiebuhua had wished to entrap him to his death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Toqto'a's western campaign, Bie'erqiebuhua had sought to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 哈麻屢言于帝，召還近地，脫脫深德之，至是引為中書右丞。

translations.literal: Hama repeatedly spoke to the emperor and had him recalled to a nearby region; Toqto'a was deeply grateful and at this time brought him in as Right Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Hama had repeatedly urged the emperor to recall Toqto'a to a nearby post. Toqto'a was deeply grateful and now appointed him Right Secretariat Councillor.

sentences.zh: 而是時脫脫信用汝中柏，由左司郎中參議中書省事，平章以下見其議事莫敢異同，惟哈麻不為之下。

translations.literal: But at this time Toqto'a trusted and employed Ru Zhongbai, who from his post as Left Department Director deliberated on Secretariat affairs; Pacification Commissioners and those below, seeing him deliberate on affairs, dared not disagree, only Hama would not defer to him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Toqto'a put his trust in Ru Zhongbai, who from his post as Left Department Director effectively ran Secretariat affairs. Officials down to the rank of Pacification Commissioner dared not contradict him — only Hama refused to bow to him.

sentences.zh: 汝中柏因譖之脫脫，改為宣政院使，位居第三，於是哈麻深銜之。

translations.literal: Ru Zhongbai therefore slandered him to Toqto'a; Hama was transferred to Commissioner of the Xuanzheng Academy, in the third rank — and so Hama deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Zhongbai slandered Hama to Toqto'a, who transferred Hama to Commissioner of the Xuanzheng Academy — a third-rank post — and Hama deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 哈麻嘗與脫脫議授皇太子冊寶禮，脫脫每言：「中宮有子將置之何所？」

translations.literal: Hama had once discussed with Toqto'a the ceremony for presenting the crown prince with the seal and regalia. Toqto'a would always say: "The empress has a son — where would you put him?
translations.idiomatic: Hama had once discussed with Toqto'a the ceremony for investing the crown prince with the seal and regalia. Toqto'a would always ask, "The empress has a son of her own — where would you place him?

sentences.zh: 以故久不行。

translations.literal: For this reason it was long not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the ceremony was long deferred.

sentences.zh: 脫脫將出師也，以汝中柏為治書侍御史，使輔也先帖木兒居中。

translations.literal: When Toqto'a was about to take the field, he made Ru Zhongbai Investigating Censor to assist Yexiantemur in holding the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Toqto'a was about to take the field, he made Ru Zhongbai Investigating Censor to assist Yexiantemur in holding the capital.

sentences.zh: 汝中柏恐哈麻必為後患，欲去之。

translations.literal: Ru Zhongbai feared Hama would surely become a future threat and wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Zhongbai feared Hama would become a future threat and wanted him removed.

sentences.zh: 脫脫猶豫未決，令與也先帖木兒謀。

translations.literal: Toqto'a hesitated and had not decided; he ordered consultation with Yexiantemur.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a hesitated and ordered Yexiantemur consulted.

sentences.zh: 也先帖木兒以其有功於己，不從。

translations.literal: Yexiantemur, because Hama had done him a service, did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Yexiantemur, because Hama had done him a service, refused.

sentences.zh: 哈麻知之，遂譖脫脫於皇太子及皇后奇氏。

translations.literal: Hama learned of this and then slandered Toqto'a to the crown prince and Empress Gi.
translations.idiomatic: Hama learned of this and slandered Toqto'a to the crown prince and Empress Gi.

sentences.zh: 會也先帖木兒方移疾家居，監察御史袁賽因不花等承哈麻風旨，上章劾之，三奏乃允；

translations.literal: Just then Yexiantemur was convalescing at home; supervising censor Yuan Saiyinbuhua and others, following Hama's veiled instruction, submitted impeachments; only after three submissions was it approved;
translations.idiomatic: Just then Yexiantemur was convalescing at home. Supervising censors Yuan Saiyinbuhua and others, acting on Hama's veiled instruction, submitted impeachments; only after three submissions was the charge approved;

sentences.zh: 奪御史臺印，出都門外聽旨，以汪家奴為御史大夫；

translations.literal: the Censorate seal was seized, and Yexiantemur was ordered to wait outside the capital gate for further orders; Wangjianu was made Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: Yexiantemur's Censorate seal was seized and he was ordered to wait outside the capital gate for further orders; Wangjianu was made Censor-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 而脫脫亦有淮安之命。

translations.literal: and Toqto'a also received the order to be confined at Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a received the same order to be confined at Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛亥，詔至軍中，參議龔伯遂曰：「將在軍，君命有所不受。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day of the twelfth month the edict reached the army. Consultant Gong Bosui said: "When the general is in the field, the sovereign's command may in some cases be refused.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day of the twelfth month the edict reached the army. Consultant Gong Bosui said, "A general in the field may disregard the sovereign's orders.

sentences.zh: 且丞相出師時，嘗被密旨，今奉密旨一意進討可也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the chief councillor set out on campaign he once received a secret edict; now obey the secret edict and press the attack with single purpose — that will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief councillor set out he received a secret edict. Obey that edict and press the attack — that is enough.

sentences.zh: 詔書且勿開，開則大事去矣。」

translations.literal: Do not yet open the edict — once opened, the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Do not open the edict yet — once opened, all is lost.

sentences.zh: 脫脫曰：「天子詔我而我不從，是與天子抗也，君臣之義何在？」

translations.literal: Toqto'a said: "The Son of Heaven has commanded me and I do not obey — this is resisting the Son of Heaven. Where then is the meaning of lord and minister?
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a said, "If the emperor commands me and I refuse, I am resisting the throne. What then becomes of the bond between sovereign and subject?

sentences.zh: 弗從。

translations.literal: He did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: He would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 既聽詔，脫脫頓首謝曰：「臣至愚，荷天子寵靈，委以軍國重事，蚤夜戰兢，懼弗能勝。

translations.literal: After hearing the edict, Toqto'a bowed his head and thanked him, saying: "Your subject is utterly foolish; bearing the Son of Heaven's gracious favor, entrusted with weighty affairs of army and state, I have been vigilant day and night, fearing I could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: After hearing the edict, Toqto'a kowtowed and said, "Your subject is utterly unworthy. Honored with the emperor's trust and charged with affairs of army and state, I have been vigilant day and night, fearing I could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 一旦釋此重負，上恩所及者深矣。」

translations.literal: To be released from this heavy burden in a single day — the sovereign's grace reaches deep indeed.
translations.idiomatic: To be released from this heavy burden in a single day — the emperor's grace is beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 即出兵甲及名馬三千，分賜諸將，俾各帥所部以聽月闊察兒、雪雪節制。

translations.literal: He thereupon brought out armor and three thousand famous horses, distributed them among the generals, and had each lead his own troops to receive the authority of Yuekuochae'r and Xuexue.
translations.idiomatic: He then distributed armor and three thousand fine horses among the generals and ordered each to lead his own troops under the command of Yuekuochae'r and Xuexue.

sentences.zh: 客省副使哈剌荅曰：「丞相此行，我輩必死他人之手，今日寧死丞相前。」

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner of the Guest Office Haracha said: "On this journey of the chief councillor, we shall surely die at others' hands — today I would rather die before the chief councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner of the Guest Office Haracha said, "On this journey we shall surely die at another's hand. Better to die before the chief councillor today.

sentences.zh: 拔刀刎頸而死。

translations.literal: He drew his sword and cut his own throat, dying.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 初命脫脫安置淮安，俄有旨移置亦集乃路。

translations.literal: At first Toqto'a was ordered confined at Huai'an; soon an edict transferred his confinement to Yizhinailu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At first Toqto'a was ordered confined at Huai'an; soon an edict transferred him to Yizhinailu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，臺臣猶以謫輕，列疏其兄弟之罪，於是詔流脫脫于雲南大理宣慰司鎮西路，流也先帖木兒于四川碉門。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year the censorial officials still considered the demotion too light and submitted a memorial listing the brothers' crimes; thereupon an edict exiled Toqto'a to Zhenxi Road under the Dali Pacification Commission of Yunnan, and exiled Yexiantemur to Diaomen in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifteenth year the censors still considered the punishment too lenient and submitted a memorial listing the brothers' crimes. An edict then exiled Toqto'a to Zhenxi Road in the Dali Pacification Commission of Yunnan and Yexiantemur to Diaomen in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 脫脫長子哈剌章，肅州安置；

translations.literal: Toqto'a's eldest son Qarajang was confined at Suzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a's eldest son Qarajang was confined at Suzhou;

sentences.zh: 次子三寶奴，蘭州安置。

translations.literal: his second son Sanbaonu was confined at Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: his second son Sanbaonu was confined at Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 家產簿錄入官。

translations.literal: The household property was inventoried and confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: The family's property was inventoried and confiscated.

sentences.zh: 脫脫行至大理騰衝，知府高惠見脫脫，欲以女事之，許築室一程外以居，雖有加害者可以無虞。

translations.literal: When Toqto'a reached Tengchong in Dali, Prefect Gao Hui saw Toqto'a and wished to give him his daughter in marriage; he promised to build a dwelling one stage's journey away for him to live in, so that even if harm came he would be without worry.
translations.idiomatic: When Toqto'a reached Tengchong in Dali, Prefect Gao Hui offered him his daughter in marriage and promised to build him a dwelling a day's journey away, where he would be safe from harm.

sentences.zh: 脫脫曰：「吾罪人也，安敢念及此！」

translations.literal: Toqto'a said: "I am a criminal — how dare I think of such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a said, "I am a condemned man — how dare I entertain such a thought!

sentences.zh: 巽辭以絕之。

translations.literal: He declined with polite words to cut off the offer.
translations.idiomatic: He declined politely but firmly.

sentences.zh: 九月，遣官移置阿輕乞之地，高惠以 脫脫前不受其女，故首發鐵甲軍圍之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month officials were dispatched to transfer him to the place called Aqingqi; Gao Hui, because Toqto'a had earlier refused his daughter, was the first to dispatch armored troops to surround him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month officials were sent to transfer him to Aqingqi. Because Toqto'a had refused his daughter, Gao Hui was the first to dispatch armored troops to surround him.

sentences.zh: 十二月己未，哈麻矯詔遣使鴆之，死，年四十二。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day of the twelfth month Hama forged an edict and sent an envoy to poison him; he died at the age of forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day of the twelfth month Hama forged an edict and sent an envoy to poison him. He died at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 訃聞中書，遣尚舍卿七十六至其地，易棺衣以殮。

translations.literal: When word of his death reached the Secretariat, they dispatched Palace Provisioner Qishi'er to his location to change the coffin and garments for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death reached the Secretariat, Palace Provisioner Qishi'er was sent to replace the coffin and shroud for burial.

sentences.zh: 脫脫儀狀雄偉，頎然出於千百人中，而器宏識遠，莫測其蘊。

translations.literal: Toqto'a's bearing and appearance were imposing and tall, standing head and shoulders above a thousand or ten thousand men, while his capacity was broad and his vision far — none could fathom his depths.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a was tall and imposing, standing head and shoulders above any crowd, with a breadth of vision none could fathom.

sentences.zh: 功施社稷而不伐，位極人臣而不驕，輕貨財，遠聲色，好賢禮士，皆出於天性。

translations.literal: He bestowed merit on the altars of soil and grain yet did not boast; he reached the pinnacle of subjecthood yet was not arrogant; he held wealth lightly, kept far from music and women, and loved the worthy and honored scholars — all sprang from his inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: He served the state without boasting, rose to the pinnacle of power without arrogance, cared little for wealth, shunned pleasure, and honored the worthy — all by nature.

sentences.zh: 至於事君之際，始終不失臣節，雖古之有道大臣，何以過之。

translations.literal: As for his service to his lord, from beginning to end he never lost the integrity of a minister — even the great ministers of old with the Way, how could they surpass him?
translations.idiomatic: In his service to the throne he never once failed in the duty of a minister — even the greatest ministers of antiquity could scarcely have surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 惟其惑於群小，急復私讎，君子譏焉。

translations.literal: Only in being deluded by petty men and hastening to settle private grudges did men of worth find fault with him.
translations.idiomatic: Only in trusting petty men and rushing to settle private scores did men of worth find fault with him.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，監察御史張沖等上章雪其冤，於是詔復脫脫官爵，并給復其家產。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year supervising censor Zhang Chong and others submitted a memorial to clear his unjust conviction; thereupon an edict restored Toqto'a's titles and ranks and also returned his household property.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Supervising Censor Zhang Chong and others submitted a memorial to clear his name. An edict then restored Toqto'a's titles and returned his family's property.

sentences.zh: 召哈剌章、三寶奴還朝。

translations.literal: Qarajang and Sanbaonu were summoned back to court.
translations.idiomatic: Qarajang and Sanbaonu were summoned back to court.

sentences.zh: 而也先帖木兒先是亦已死，乃授哈剌章中書平章政事，封申國公，分省大同；

translations.literal: Yexiantemur, however, had already died by then; Qarajang was thereupon appointed Secretariat Pacification Commissioner, enfeoffed as Duke of Shen, and assigned to the branch secretariat at Datong;
translations.idiomatic: Yexiantemur had already died by then. Qarajang was appointed Secretariat Pacification Commissioner, enfeoffed as Duke of Shen, and posted to the branch secretariat at Datong;

sentences.zh: 三寶奴知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Sanbaonu was made Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sanbaonu was made Administrator of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，監察御史聖奴、也先、撒都失里等復言：「奸邪構害大臣，以致臨敵易將，我國家兵機不振從此始，錢糧之耗從此始，盜賊縱橫從此始，生民之塗炭從此始。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year supervising censors Shengnu, Yeshi, Sadushili, and others again said: "Wicked men framed and harmed a great minister, causing the replacement of the general on the eve of battle — from this our state's military vigor began to fail, from this the drain on treasury and grain began, from this bandits ran rampant, from this the common people began to suffer torment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year Supervising Censors Shengnu, Yeshi, Sadushili, and others memorialized again: "Wicked men framed a great minister and replaced the general on the eve of battle — from that moment our armies lost their edge, the treasury began to bleed, bandits ran rampant, and the people began to suffer.

sentences.zh: 設使脫脫不死，安得天下有今日之亂哉！

translations.literal: If Toqto'a had not died, how could the realm have the chaos of today!
translations.idiomatic: Had Toqto'a lived, how could the realm have fallen into today's chaos!

sentences.zh: 乞封一字王爵，定諡及加功臣之號。」

translations.literal: We beg that he be enfeoffed with a princely title of one character, that a posthumous title be fixed, and that the designation of meritorious minister be added.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that he be granted a princely title, a posthumous name, and the designation of meritorious minister.

sentences.zh: 朝廷皆是其言。

translations.literal: The court approved all their words.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the memorial in full.

sentences.zh: 然以國家多故，未及報而國亡。

translations.literal: Yet because the state had many troubles, before the response could be issued the dynasty perished.
translations.idiomatic: But the state was beset by crises, and before the honors could be granted the dynasty fell.
